a33.speaker: White House (US Strategy Toward Sub-Saharan Africa white paper)
a33.name: White House (US Strategy Toward Sub-Saharan Africa white paper)
a33.speech: Stated that US goals for its Africa policies were to strengthen democratic institutions, spur economic growth, trade and investment, advance peace and security, and promote opportunity and development. "across all [these] objectives, we will: deepen our engagement with Africa's young leaders; seek to empower marginalized populations and women; address the unique needs of fragile and post-conflict states; and work closely with the UN and other multilateral actors to achieve our objectives on the continent."

a33.speaker: Hillary Clinton, US Secretary of State
a33.name: Hillary Clinton
a33.title: US Secretary of State
a33.speech: At the US-SA business partnership conference: "We want sustainable partnerships in Africa that add value rather than extract it. And one of the ways we are building those partnerships is to look to enhancing and strengthening the ties between American businesses and African businesses because, as we look across Sub-Saharan Africa, we see enormous economic growth even as the global economy continues to struggle. Seven of the world's 10 fastest-growing economies are in this region."

a33.speaker: Hillary Clinton, US Secretary of State
a33.name: Hillary Clinton
a33.title: US Secretary of State
a33.speech: At the University of the Western Cape, on South Africa's leadership role: "I've often heard it said that African problems need African solutions. Well, I'm here to say that some of our global problems need African solutions too. And few nations on this continent can carry as much weight or be as effective partners and leaders as South Africa." ; "You are a democratic power with the opportunity to influence Africa and the world. You have led on non-proliferation at the International Atomic Energy Agency and on climate change at the Durban conference. You've led on economic cooperation at the G-20. You've led on women's participation in politics... But respectfully, I say that we and you can, should, and must do more."

a33.speaker: Hillary Clinton, US Secretary of State
a33.name: Hillary Clinton
a33.title: US Secretary of State
a33.speech: On Syria: "I hope that we will look at the urgent tasks that I think confront the people of Syria and the international community and think through how we can address them. First, we must figure out ways to hasten the day when the bloodshed ends and the political transition begins." She noted she would be going to Istanbul to discuss these issues with Turkey before returning to Washington.

a33.speaker: Barack Obama, US President (quoted from his Accra speech)
a33.name: Barack Obama
a33.title: US President (quoted from his Accra speech)
a33.speech: "the true sign of success is not whether we are a source of perpetual aid that helps people scrape by. It's whether we are partners in building the capacity for transformational change."

a33.speaker: Unnamed South African politician (anonymous)
a33.name: Unnamed South African politician (anonymous)
a33.speech: Told The Daily Maverick that he had been "especially impressed by Hillary's clear attempt to distance herself from any perception of the US as empire building. Her reference to the idea that the world needs African ideas to succeed was telling. It was the right message for the time."

a85.speaker: Devon Steenkamp, Ward 134 Councillor, Johannesburg
a85.name: Devon Steenkamp
a85.title: Ward 134 Councillor, Johannesburg
a85.speech: Said Johannesburg Water was assessing the damage to see if it could be done in-house or if it needed a contractor. Posted on social media (X/Twitter): "Joburg Water has been notified of a major burst at the Honeydew Reservoir again, causing serious flooding to neighboring properties. Please stock up on…" ; "The pipe is still broken. It is smaller than the one that burst last week. It runs horizontally and deteriorated [since it burst]. The problem is that even on bypass, the water pressure is not high enough to reach the high-lying areas," he said. Said despite residents being told there was alternative water supply by water tankers, the tankers had not yet been seen in the area.

a85.speaker: Johannesburg Water
a85.name: Johannesburg Water
a85.speech: Did not immediately provide comment to News24, as the communications team were in a meeting; response to be added once received. In a notice to residents, said the Honeydew Tower was empty at 10:00 and stated: "The team is on the ground assessing the damage and investigating the possibility of supplying water through the bypass. Alternative water supply will be arranged for affected areas."

a85.speaker: Dr Ferrial Adam, WaterCAN Executive Manager
a85.name: Dr Ferrial Adam
a85.title: WaterCAN Executive Manager
a85.speech: Said it was "infuriating" that Johannesburg Water had only just disclosed the extent of the reservoir leaks. Said they were relieved to finally get answers after requesting information regarding the extent of the leaks in October 2023 and May 2024. Added: "The City loses 46.1% of its potable water to non-revenue water - water lost without being paid for, 35% of this is physical loss through leaks, and the rest is water given away or stolen."

a85.speaker: Michael Crichton, Democratic Alliance Johannesburg Caucus Deputy Chair
a85.name: Michael Crichton
a85.title: Democratic Alliance Johannesburg Caucus Deputy Chair
a85.speech: "The DA in Johannesburg has taken this issue up with Johannesburg Water, but they have been vague at best with their explanation. They have informed us of poor supply coming from Rand Water's side and that there's 'high consumption'," Crichton said. Added that it was concerning that the South Hills Tower "seems to be one of the worst affected water towers." Said: "What is also of concern is that Rand Water's Meyershill reservoir has been out of commission for the past two to three years." Said the community had been fighting the issue for four years, and that the caucus would submit questions for MMC Jack Sekwaila to answer and would submit a PAIA application, "and we will be bringing a motion to Council demanding a full investigation into this crisis which will include, but not be limited to, engaging the National Government on a long-term solution."

a201.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO) (statement)
a201.name: World Health Organization (WHO) (statement)
a201.speech: Says the recent surge in violence in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo has led to significant loss of life, trauma, displacement, and the destruction of critical health infrastructure, exacerbating an already dire situation for millions of people; the situation remains tense and volatile, and the health needs are immense. WHO remains on the ground, and has continued to respond to the health needs by providing lifesaving medical supplies, supporting health workers, and coordinating the emergency response.

a201.speaker: 31 health facilities in and around Goma, North Kivu (reports)
a201.name: 31 health facilities in and around Goma
a201.title: North Kivu (reports)
a201.speech: Since 26 January, 3082 injured and 843 dead have been reported from 31 health facilities in and around Goma, North Kivu; with the alarming expansion of violence further south, 65 injuries were reported from 3 hospitals in South Kivu.

a201.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO) (statement)
a201.name: World Health Organization (WHO) (statement)
a201.speech: Reports that over 70 (or 6%) of the health facilities in North Kivu have been affected, with some completely destroyed and others struggling to restart operations; some ambulances have also been damaged; a WHO-supported health clinic in North Kivu was temporarily occupied by armed groups; health workers have had to flee in places, while in others, they have been working round the clock for days, with limited resources and overwhelming demand, and sometimes at risk to their own lives.

a201.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO) (statement)
a201.name: World Health Organization (WHO) (statement)
a201.speech: Warns that the threat of infectious diseases has multiplied, with cholera, malaria, measles, meningitis, mpox and tuberculosis among the infectious threats in the area; close to 600 suspected cases of cholera and 14 deaths were reported from North Kivu between 1 and 27 January; ninety percent of the mpox patients (128 of 143) in isolation units in Goma had fled for safety, making it nearly impossible to provide them with care, and increasing the risk of spread.

a201.speaker: Rapid assessment of 10 healthcare facilities in and around Goma
a201.name: Rapid assessment of 10 healthcare facilities in and around Goma
a201.speech: Showed a concerning rise in rape and other gender-based violence: there were 45 cases reported among the displaced, and 21 survivors of gang-rape admitted to two hospitals. These numbers are only the tip of the iceberg.

a201.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO) (statement)
a201.name: World Health Organization (WHO) (statement)
a201.speech: Says it has deployed emergency medical supplies, hygiene and water treatment supplies, and tents to increase hospital capacity by 1000 beds; supplies are being depleted rapidly, and more resources are urgently needed; WHO is preparing further deliveries as part of an ECHO-led effort to fly in critical supplies, for which the Goma airport, a critical lifeline, must be urgently reopened; WHO has spent US$ 600 000 to meet immediate health needs while the overall response requires US$ 50 million.

a201.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO) (statement)
a201.name: World Health Organization (WHO) (statement)
a201.speech: Says the United States’ recent decision to freeze foreign aid is significantly impacting relief efforts in the Democratic Republic of the Congo; last year, the US contributed to as much as 70% of the country’s humanitarian response, and the US is a major funder of the mpox response, having pledged a million vaccine doses of its own stock to global efforts; while WHO’s humanitarian response in the region relies on funding from other donors—including the European Union, United Kingdom and the WHO’s Contingency Fund for Emergencies—reductions in overall aid will have repercussions on people’s health.

a201.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO) (statement)
a201.name: World Health Organization (WHO) (statement)
a201.speech: Calls for humanitarian access, the protection of health workers and facilities, and an end to attacks on health care. Health facilities, supplies, workers and patients should be protected. “Ultimately, we call for peace, and an end to the unimaginable and long suffering of the people in this region.”

a201.speaker: WHO Director-General
a201.name: WHO Director-General
a201.speech: Declared a public health emergency of international concern last August over the mpox outbreak, whose epicentre is eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, especially South Kivu province.

a300.speaker: A source (anonymous)
a300.name: A source (anonymous)
a300.speech: Told this publication that instead of being rejected as per the standards, the aspiring teachers are advised to restart to attain the required minimum qualifications while they pursue the tertiary qualifications simultaneously.

a300.speaker: Nanikie Mnisi, Principal Secretary in the Ministry of Education and Training
a300.name: Nanikie Mnisi
a300.title: Principal Secretary in the Ministry of Education and Training
a300.speech: Revealed that the ministry was aware of this anomaly and declared that these teachers were indeed unemployable.

a300.speaker: Nanikie Mnisi, Principal Secretary in the Ministry of Education and Training
a300.name: Nanikie Mnisi
a300.title: Principal Secretary in the Ministry of Education and Training
a300.speech: Revealed that the consequences for higher learning institutions found wanting on the EQA standards is automatic shutdown; said the ministry will examine this anomaly and act accordingly.

a364.speaker: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC)
a364.name: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC)
a364.speech: Announced on Saturday that it has successfully shut down more than 11,000 drug shops nationwide and confiscated counterfeit drugs valued in the trillions.

a364.speaker: NAFDAC Director-General (unnamed, referred to as "she")
a364.name: NAFDAC Director-General (unnamed
a364.title: referred to as "she")
a364.speech: Regretted that NAFDAC's findings during the operation have been alarming.

a405.speaker: Prof. Mohamed Yakub Janabi, candidate for WHO Regional Director for Africa
a405.name: Prof. Mohamed Yakub Janabi
a405.title: candidate for WHO Regional Director for Africa
a405.speech: “Africa's health challenges are unique, and our solutions must be homegrown,” Janabi said in his election manifesto. His policy platform emphasizes universal health coverage, emergency preparedness, and stronger regional cooperation. He has pledged to modernize WHO-AFRO's operations by making the organization more accountable, efficient, and responsive to member states' needs.

a405.speaker: Prof. Mohamed Yakub Janabi, candidate for WHO Regional Director for Africa
a405.name: Prof. Mohamed Yakub Janabi
a405.title: candidate for WHO Regional Director for Africa
a405.speech: Argues that universal health coverage should be seen not as an expense but as an investment in Africa's long-term prosperity; he points to his work in Tanzania, where targeted health investments have significantly reduced maternal mortality and increased access to specialized medical care; he has proposed innovative financing mechanisms, including debt swaps and regional investment funds, to reduce dependence on foreign aid ; if elected, he promises a leadership style that is inclusive, action-oriented, and deeply committed to improving lives across the continent.

a405.speaker: Senior Tanzanian health official (anonymous)
a405.name: Senior Tanzanian health official (anonymous)
a405.speech: “Janabi understands both the science and the politics of healthcare. That's exactly what Africa needs right now.”

a470.speaker: Dolly Parton, singer
a470.name: Dolly Parton
a470.title: singer
a470.speech: Asked if her husband Carl Dean had a favorite outfit of hers, Parton remembered: “I used to have a pair of a pair of red velvet hot pants back when…”

a702.speaker: Médecins Sans Frontières/Doctors Without Borders (MSF)
a702.name: Médecins Sans Frontières/Doctors Without Borders (MSF)
a702.speech: Calls on all armed actors to actively ensure the protection of civilians, humanitarian workers and medical facilities from the ongoing violence.

a702.speaker: Víctor García Leonor, MSF head of operations for Mozambique
a702.name: Víctor García Leonor
a702.title: MSF head of operations for Mozambique
a702.speech: "We are deeply concerned about the escalating violence and its direct impact on every aspect of people's lives, including access to healthcare." ; "Hundreds of thousands of people are in dire need of medical and humanitarian assistance in Cabo Delgado. But insecurity is continuously cutting them off from reaching it. This results in preventable deaths and suffering."

a702.speaker: Víctor García Leonor, MSF head of operations for Mozambique
a702.name: Víctor García Leonor
a702.title: MSF head of operations for Mozambique
a702.speech: "MSF remains committed to standing by the people of Cabo Delgado and to resume activities in Mocímboa da Praia as soon as we obtain guarantees that our staff will be able to work in a safe manner." ; "Time and again we call on all armed actors and stakeholders to protect civilians, medical facilities and humanitarian workers from violence." ; "Safe and unhindered access to healthcare is vital for communities caught in conflict and their freedom of movement should be guaranteed when they are seeking protection."

a870.speaker: Ibrahim Héma, Executive Secretary of the Orange Burkina Faso Foundation
a870.name: Ibrahim Héma
a870.title: Executive Secretary of the Orange Burkina Faso Foundation
a870.speech: Said this ambitious project aims to address the acute need for blood, especially at certain times of the year ; “Very often, lives are lost for lack of available blood. That is why the Orange Foundation, faithful to its commitment to accessible and supportive healthcare, is resolutely committed to responding to this urgent need by mobilising our forces and our resources to save lives.” ; added that beyond the collection, this initiative is a call for national solidarity: “Giving your blood is offering a second chance to a mother in difficulty, to a sick child, or to a road accident victim. It is a gesture of fraternity accessible to all of us.”

a870.speaker: Ibrahim Héma, Executive Secretary of the Orange Burkina Faso Foundation
a870.name: Ibrahim Héma
a870.title: Executive Secretary of the Orange Burkina Faso Foundation
a870.speech: Explained the actions planned to reach the target of 1,000 bags of blood: “Two days before the collection, an awareness campaign is carried out at the different sites. Teams from the National Blood Transfusion Centre (CNTS) and volunteers tour the sites to raise awareness among the population. On the day of the collection, a CNTS team travels with the Orange Burkina Faso outreach team to continue raising awareness and inviting people to come and give their blood.”

a870.speaker: Narcisse Naré, chargé de mission of the Minister of Health
a870.name: Narcisse Naré
a870.title: chargé de mission of the Minister of Health
a870.speech: Recalled that according to the CNTS 2024 report, the rate of satisfaction of blood needs was 66.28 percent, a figure which calls for more action and commitment to fill the shortage ; “This campaign organised by the Orange Burkina Faso Foundation aims to collect about (1,000) bags of blood, which will help guarantee the availability of blood in our health centres for the benefit of our patients. It therefore constitutes a real hope for all those who need blood to recover their health.”

a870.speaker: CNTS (National Blood Transfusion Centre) 2024 report
a870.name: CNTS (National Blood Transfusion Centre) 2024 report
a870.speech: Reported that the rate of satisfaction of blood needs was 66.28 percent.

a995.speaker: Institute for Security Studies (ISS) study on digital disinformation during the 2024 elections
a995.name: Institute for Security Studies (ISS) study on digital disinformation during the 2024 elections
a995.speech: Reveals that the Electoral Commission of South Africa (IEC) and other democratic institutions were primary targets for coordinated campaigns promoting false narratives, and shows how the role of network affiliations across Africa appears to be growing in importance. The year-long study found that key figures in South Africa’s influence industry were engaged in transnational coordinated campaigns, including so-called rage bait; and that from a sample of 1.2 million documents on X and over 177,000 on Facebook, the uMkhonto weSizwe (MK) and Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) parties were the ‘loudest’ voices on the platforms, both of which ‘had an outsized effect on the conversation given their final election results’ and ‘appear to have benefitted from paid influencers including those ideologically aligned to the party.’ The report observed of the Democratic Alliance’s traditional political advertising that ‘these ads are transparent […] it is clear which political party is paying for them, allowing voters to assess the narrative in that light.’ It also found that fact-checking organisations and the traditional media played a significant role in debunking disinformation during South Africa’s elections.

a995.speaker: One of South Africa’s top online political influencers (anonymous)
a995.name: One of South Africa’s top online political influencers (anonymous)
a995.speech: Told the ISS how he engaged with the Kenyan X community before the polls using antagonistic, often nationalist-themed interactions to ‘provoke reactions’ on South Africa-Kenyan rivalries, so that he could appropriate networks and build his audience based on negative engagement. He said he was embarking on similar tactics in Botswana, Zimbabwe and Nigeria.

a995.speaker: Another prominent South African influencer (anonymous)
a995.name: Another prominent South African influencer (anonymous)
a995.speech: Claimed Russian agents paid him to amplify narratives aimed at ‘destabilising’ South Africa during the polls, and said he was provided with pre-packaged material and paid up to R50 ($US2.7) each time he liked a post.

a995.speaker: IEC and Government Communication and Information Service representatives
a995.name: IEC and Government Communication and Information Service representatives
a995.speech: Said at a recent conference to discuss the study that despite efforts to mitigate such campaigns, mis/disinformation flourished. The conference noted that the rise of artificial intelligence and the rapid spread of disinformation would probably make such campaigns harder to track, with a noticeable shift towards smaller, localised networks such as WhatsApp.

a995.speaker: Meta
a995.name: Meta
a995.speech: Plans to end fact-checking by third parties, so content warnings by the platform, like those of Africa Check during the election, could become history.

a995.speaker: Aldu Cornelissen, part of the ISS research team
a995.name: Aldu Cornelissen
a995.title: part of the ISS research team
a995.speech: Said at the Cape Town conference that since the Ukraine invasion, ‘we are seeing the American right being pulled into influence campaigns.’

a995.speaker: Elon Musk
a995.name: Elon Musk
a995.speech: Spread false narratives in early February about land expropriation, which the article suggests may have been a clumsy stunt to justify subsequent US aid cuts to South Africa.

a995.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a995.name: Donald Trump
a995.title: US President
a995.speech: Issued a recent executive order to ‘stop government censorship’ on social media.

a1118.speaker: Michael Raynor, United States Ambassador to Benin
a1118.name: Michael Raynor
a1118.title: United States Ambassador to Benin
a1118.speech: Did not fail to express his gratitude to the government and the people of Benin for the good times he was able to spend during his three years of service in Benin: "I am truly honoured to have represented my country here for three years. I had the privilege of discovering the many riches of this country and I was above all impressed by the dynamism of the women and young people of Benin." He gave assurances that his departure would change nothing in the bilateral cooperation between the United States and Benin, cooperation which he tried to strengthen during his stay in Cotonou.

a1118.speaker: Boni Yayi, President of the Republic of Benin
a1118.name: Boni Yayi
a1118.title: President of the Republic of Benin
a1118.speech: Made a point of saluting "a great friend" of Benin who shares with the United States the values of the free world: "For three years, you accepted our shortcomings, you accompanied us in our reforms."

a1118.speaker: Boni Yayi, President of the Republic of Benin
a1118.name: Boni Yayi
a1118.title: President of the Republic of Benin
a1118.speech: For him, the Beninese people are attached to democracy, which does not go together with poverty: "The gap between poverty and democracy must be avoided. If poverty is severe, it betrays democracy. Likewise, democracy does not go together with a failing education system, inadequate health services, or a deficit in infrastructure, primarily energy."

a1118.speaker: Boni Yayi, President of the Republic of Benin
a1118.name: Boni Yayi
a1118.title: President of the Republic of Benin
a1118.speech: Saluted the American diplomat's involvement in securing the second Millennium Challenge Account compact, whose total financing amounts to an estimated $411 million, or more than 200 billion CFA francs: "It is the first time that a country has received an amount higher than what it received under the first compact," said the President of the Republic, who assured the United States of his government's determination to improve governance.

a1307.speaker: Confederation of Sahel States (AES) (decision announced in Bamako)
a1307.name: Confederation of Sahel States (AES) (decision announced in Bamako)
a1307.speech: Decided on 28 March in Bamako that products imported from countries that are not members of the Alliance will be charged a confederal tax of 0.5% of their customs value. The measure is intended to create an autonomous AES budget, without dependence on foreign aid or national contributions, with the funds going to support for the Union's institutions, the development of regional projects, and the creation of a future AES Investment Bank. The tax will not apply to products manufactured within the AES, to hydrocarbons, humanitarian aid, diplomatic cargo, or travellers' personal effects. The funds will be accumulated in single accounts in the participating countries and their distribution entrusted to the presiding state, currently Mali, led by Assimi Goïta.

a1434.speaker: United States Supreme Court (5-4 majority ruling)
a1434.name: United States Supreme Court (5-4 majority ruling)
a1434.speech: In a 5-4 ruling, rejected an effort by the Trump administration to block the payment of $2 billion in foreign aid, upholding a lower court ruling that required the administration to proceed with payments on completed contracts; according to the ruling, the federal judge who initially ordered the resumption of payments for contracts involving USAID and the State Department "should clarify what obligations the Government must fulfill," the majority opinion stated.

a1434.speaker: Justice Samuel Alito, US Supreme Court (dissenting opinion, joined by the court's three other conservative justices)
a1434.name: Justice Samuel Alito
a1434.title: US Supreme Court (dissenting opinion, joined by the court's three other conservative justices)
a1434.speech: The dissenting justices questioned whether a single district court judge had the authority to compel such payments. "Does a single district-court judge, who likely lacks jurisdiction, have the unchecked power to compel the Government of the United States to pay out (and probably lose forever) $2 billion in taxpayer dollars?" Alito wrote in his dissent. "The answer to that question should be an emphatic 'No,' but a majority of this Court apparently thinks otherwise. I am stunned," he added.

a1434.speaker: DW (Deutsche Welle)
a1434.name: DW (Deutsche Welle)
a1434.speech: Reports that Chief Justice John Roberts and Justice Amy Coney Barrett, a Trump appointee, joined the court's three liberal justices in the majority.

a1434.speaker: District Judge Amir Ali, appointee of former President Joe Biden
a1434.name: District Judge Amir Ali
a1434.title: appointee of former President Joe Biden
a1434.speech: Had issued a temporary restraining order last month prohibiting the Trump administration from "suspending, pausing, or otherwise preventing" the disbursement of foreign aid funds.

a1434.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a1434.name: Donald Trump
a1434.title: US President
a1434.speech: Has previously described USAID as being "run by radical lunatics".

a1714.speaker: Traditional leaders of the stranded South Sudanese in Khartoum
a1714.name: Traditional leaders of the stranded South Sudanese in Khartoum
a1714.speech: Have said at least 700 South Sudanese nationals stranded in the Sudanese capital Khartoum are in a dire humanitarian situation and require urgent and coordinated assistance to return to their country.

a1714.speaker: Othow Ajak, Paramount Chief
a1714.name: Othow Ajak
a1714.title: Paramount Chief
a1714.speech: Said his people are currently living in difficult condition with inadequate basic necessities and the threat that the constant fighting poses to their safety. "We appeal to the government, citizens of South Sudan in the diaspora, and compassionate hearts to help us leave Khartoum for South Sudan," Othow said in an interview with Eye Radio on Saturday. "We are currently living in harsh conditions here, and we hope you will save us. We are living here with about 700 citizens, and with us are the elderly, a large number of children, widows, and the sick." ; He said the refugees can hardly afford to eat due to the limited access to humanitarian assistance, while there is currently no safe passage out of Khartoum: "As the war continues and we do not know when it will end, we are in difficult situation. We do not even have money. We need [help] to support us and transfer us from Khartoum to South Sudan."

a1714.speaker: Khames Dak, local chief
a1714.name: Khames Dak
a1714.title: local chief
a1714.speech: Describes the refugees' situation as miserable due to a lack of food, shelter, and means of income. "We are in a miserable situation. We live without shelter or food. Even the simple jobs that used to be available are not longer there. The war has continued for the second year, we suffer from diseases and our children are not in school." ; "Even the women who used to work as tea sellers have suffered from beatings and robberies. We appeal for support to get out of this predicament. We do not own anything."

a1753.speaker: Agriculture Innovation Mechanism for Scale (AIM for Scale) / Global Partnership to Scale-Up Weather Services for Farmers (statement)
a1753.name: Agriculture Innovation Mechanism for Scale (AIM for Scale) / Global Partnership to Scale-Up Weather Services for Farmers (statement)
a1753.speech: According to a statement on Thursday, a consortium of global partners committed to mobilizing significant investments totaling more than One Billion United States Dollars over the next three years to drive the implementation of the AIM for Scale Weather Package.

a1753.speaker: Professor Charles Anosike, Director General and Chief Executive Officer of the Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NiMet) and Permanent Representative of Nigeria with the WMO
a1753.name: Professor Charles Anosike
a1753.title: Director General and Chief Executive Officer of the Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NiMet) and Permanent Representative of Nigeria with the WMO
a1753.speech: Representing the WMO community, shared experiences of NiMet's Seasonal Climate Prediction (SCP), and ongoing projects funded by the Gates Foundation in support of scaling up weather services for millions of farmers in Nigeria. "I am looking forward to strengthening our agrometeorological systems to support #EW4ALL in Nigeria at the Nigerian Meteorological Agency."

a1753.speaker: Dr. Amna al Dahak, Minister for Climate Change and Environment of the UAE
a1753.name: Dr. Amna al Dahak
a1753.title: Minister for Climate Change and Environment of the UAE
a1753.speech: Welcomed the launch of AIM for Scale following the achievements of the AIM for Climate platform, saying: "Today, with the launch of AIM for Scale, we are accelerating our efforts to find highly promising, climate-friendly agricultural innovations and breaking down barriers to their scaling."

a1753.speaker: Michael Kremer, Nobel laureate, Chair of the Innovation Commission for Climate Change, Food Security, and Agriculture and Chair of AIM for Scale's Advisory Panel
a1753.name: Michael Kremer
a1753.title: Nobel laureate, Chair of the Innovation Commission for Climate Change, Food Security, and Agriculture and Chair of AIM for Scale's Advisory Panel
a1753.speech: Highlighted the significance of these investments: "There is a wealth of evidence that smallholder farmers benefit from high-quality weather forecasts. Yet, the challenge of reaching hundreds of millions of farmers remains. AIM for Scale is a vital step toward filling this gap by leveraging new investments and global partnerships."

a2023.speaker: Peter H. Vrooman, U.S. Ambassador to Mozambique
a2023.name: Peter H. Vrooman
a2023.title: U.S. Ambassador to Mozambique
a2023.speech: After laying the first brick at the groundbreaking ceremony, said, "We are committing today to build a modern school that will meet the needs of all children of this community. Today's signing marks a significant milestone in our joint efforts to promote education for youth and resilience in northern Mozambique."

a2023.speaker: Peter H. Vrooman, U.S. Ambassador to Mozambique
a2023.name: Peter H. Vrooman
a2023.title: U.S. Ambassador to Mozambique
a2023.speech: Said in his remarks: "It is an honor to be here today to enhance the strong partnership between the Government of the United States of America and the Government of Mozambique, through the Ministry of Education and Human Development. At this site in particular, this partnership will provide access to education for up to 4,500 students annually, improving and strengthening the education sector in Cabo Delgado Province. We are proud to be here today to see the beginning of construction of the Maringanha Secondary School and to sign the Memorandum of Understanding with the Ministry."

a2023.speaker: Peter H. Vrooman, U.S. Ambassador to Mozambique
a2023.name: Peter H. Vrooman
a2023.title: U.S. Ambassador to Mozambique
a2023.speech: Said: "The ongoing conflict in the region has resulted in the flight of nearly 18,000 internally displaced students to the city of Pemba, causing further pressure on the already stressed educational infrastructure. Today we are here with the Ministry of Education to bring solutions to this challenge." ; "Young people without access to education or job opportunities have been one of the most vulnerable targets to enlisting violent extremist groups. I am therefore happy to join our Mozambican and US teams in the effort to build the Maringanha Secondary School. The construction of the school will include local laborers for up to 40% of the workforce. We envision that these workers and these students will be less vulnerable to these extremist groups and better able to move forward into building a bright future for Cabo Delgado."

a2023.speaker: Peter H. Vrooman, U.S. Ambassador to Mozambique
a2023.name: Peter H. Vrooman
a2023.title: U.S. Ambassador to Mozambique
a2023.speech: Said: "The U.S. Government has so far committed $6.6 million to this project through the new 10-year strategy to prevent conflict and promote stability in Mozambique. This strategy supports the Government of Mozambique's efforts in the reconstruction of critical infrastructure, as prioritized in the Government's Cabo Delgado Reconstruction Plan."

a2023.speaker: Peter H. Vrooman, U.S. Ambassador to Mozambique
a2023.name: Peter H. Vrooman
a2023.title: U.S. Ambassador to Mozambique
a2023.speech: Said: "Although we are just beginning the implementation of this project, we know that the people of Cabo Delgado no longer want to hear speeches. They want physical evidence of our work to improve their current situation. So my appeal is for all of us to celebrate now, but then to quickly roll up our sleeves and start working on full implementation." ; "The construction of the Maringanha Secondary School in Pemba is a physical demonstration of the commitment of the American people to Mozambique. We are here today as a sign of our successful bilateral partnership in the education sector. This is a day for us to celebrate!" ; "This gift from the American people is an investment in the Mozambican people. We look forward to continuing to work closely with you in the future. Obrigado e estamos juntos!"

a2188.speaker: World Bank
a2188.name: World Bank
a2188.speech: For its 2025/26 financial year, considers 22 African countries to be low-income, with a gross national income (GNI) per person equivalent to or below $1,145; considers 23 African countries lower-middle-income and eight upper-middle-income.

a2188.speaker: World Bank
a2188.name: World Bank
a2188.speech: Suggests the African Continental Free Trade Area's (AfCFTA) implementation could boost FDI by up to 120 per cent, with intra-African investment also rising by about 85 per cent.

a2188.speaker: African Futures and Innovation, Institute for Security Studies (Financial Flows theme, International Futures forecasting platform)
a2188.name: African Futures and Innovation
a2188.title: Institute for Security Studies (Financial Flows theme, International Futures forecasting platform)
a2188.speech: Examines the effect on Africa of increased FDI, remittances and aid in a post-Donald Trump world, compared to a business-as-usual forecast; models inward FDI increasing to 5.3 per cent of GDP ($351 billion vs $230 billion) by 2043, with Africa's GDP $243.5 billion larger and average GDP per capita $160 higher than the business-as-usual forecast, and extreme poverty declining by one percentage point.

a2252.speaker: Thrive by Five Index (survey of preschool child development)
a2252.name: Thrive by Five Index (survey of preschool child development)
a2252.speech: A new survey, the largest ever conducted in SA, has found that 65% of 4-5 year-old children attending Early Learning Programmes (ELPs) in South Africa are lagging behind physically ; according to South Africa's largest ever survey of preschool child development, the Thrive by Five Index, in which more than 5 000 children aged 4-5 years enrolled in various types of ELPs around the country were assessed in three areas, many children are not meeting the expected early learning and/or physical growth standards for their age and will start Grade R at a considerable disadvantage, with possible long term implications for their education ; the Index reports that 55% of children attending ELPs are not able to do the learning tasks expected of children their age, with 28% of children falling far behind the expected standard ; the Index found that 27.5% of children did not meet the standard when it came to age-appropriate social relations with peers and adults, while 33.4% were found to not be emotionally ready for school ; the Index found that while there are instances of considerable variation in performance within income groups, on average children from poorer households are falling behind their better off peers as a result of the challenges they face in their earliest years.

a2252.speaker: The Thrive by Five Index partnership
a2252.name: The Thrive by Five Index partnership
a2252.speech: Has called for urgent collective action to decrease the performance gap between young children in the richest and poorest households at the point of entry into school; and to increase the percentage of young children in South Africa who thrive by five, setting more children up for success.

a2252.speaker: Angie Motshekga, Basic Education Minister
a2252.name: Angie Motshekga
a2252.title: Basic Education Minister
a2252.speech: "The Thrive by Five Index has truly thrown into sharp focus the importance of the work of ECD in moulding and shaping the nation's future leaders, moreover the index will enable the DBE to track progress in providing integrated services that lead to improved child outcomes over the next 10 years."

a2310.speaker: Africa Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC)
a2310.name: Africa Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC)
a2310.speech: says millions of lives across the continent are at risk due to abrupt cuts in U.S. and European development aid, threatening to reverse decades of progress in global health.

a2310.speaker: Dr Jean Kaseya, Director-General of the Africa CDC
a2310.name: Dr Jean Kaseya
a2310.title: Director-General of the Africa CDC
a2310.speech: made this known at the bi-weekly media webinar news conference on Thursday: "As the U.S. Congress prepares to debate the reauthorisation of the President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) on March 25, millions of lives in Africa hang in the balance," he said ; Kaseya has sounded the alarm on what he called a "total disaster" for the continent’s health sector.

a2310.speaker: Dr Jean Kaseya, Director-General of the Africa CDC
a2310.name: Dr Jean Kaseya
a2310.title: Director-General of the Africa CDC
a2310.speech: He said that 30 per cent of Africa’s health expenditure comes from Official Development Assistance (ODA): "This year, the ODA funding has been slashed by 70 per cent, dropping from 81 billion dollars to just 25 billion dollars." ; "Beyond HIV/AIDS, the funding crisis comes amid a surge in disease outbreaks across Africa—up 41 per cent in the past two years." ; "In the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), the loss of USAID funding has disrupted Mpox testing, leading to a 16 per cent drop in confirmed cases not because the outbreak is under control, but due to a lack of resources to track it. The turnaround time for testing has also increased in many regions due to logistical challenges," he said.

a2310.speaker: Dr Jean Kaseya, Director-General of the Africa CDC
a2310.name: Dr Jean Kaseya
a2310.title: Director-General of the Africa CDC
a2310.speech: said that the aid cuts threaten to undo 20 years of progress in maternal and child health, infectious disease control, and poverty reduction; with donor funding disappearing, he said, the entire health systems could collapse, and millions more Africans could be pushed into extreme poverty ; "Africa CDC projects that 39 million people will be driven into poverty as a direct result of these funding cuts," he said.

a2310.speaker: Dr Jean Kaseya, Director-General of the Africa CDC
a2310.name: Dr Jean Kaseya
a2310.title: Director-General of the Africa CDC
a2310.speech: said that health financing remains a persistent challenge: "Only two African countries Botswana and Rwanda meet the Abuja Declaration’s commitment to spend 15 per cent of GDP on health. Only 16 countries have national health financing plans in place. Without external funding, many nations are struggling to keep their health services afloat," he said.

a2310.speaker: Dr Jean Kaseya, Director-General of the Africa CDC
a2310.name: Dr Jean Kaseya
a2310.title: Director-General of the Africa CDC
a2310.speech: said he has been meeting with ministers and the African Union to push for increased domestic investment in health and explore "blended financing" strategies involving the private sector: "One innovative proposal involves leveraging the 95 billion dollars in annual remittances from the African diaspora, potentially through a taxation model to fund healthcare initiatives. With limited time to act, I will be meeting with members of the Trump administration, PEPFAR officials, and U.S. lawmakers to make the case for continued aid," he said.

a2310.speaker: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a2310.name: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a2310.speech: said the Trump administration’s decision to pause U.S. foreign aid has "substantially disrupted" supply of HIV treatments in eight countries, which could soon run out of these life-saving medicines; the global health agency said that Haiti, Kenya, Lesotho, South Sudan, Burkina Faso, Mali, Nigeria and Ukraine could exhaust their supply of HIV treatments in the coming months ; The WHO said the U.S. has a "responsibility to ensure that if it withdraws direct funding for countries, it’s done in an orderly and humane way that allows them to find alternative sources of funding."

a2310.speaker: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a2310.name: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a2310.speech: said funding shortages could also force 80 per cent of its supported essential health care services in Afghanistan to close; as of March 4, the WHO said, 167 health facilities had shut down due to funding shortages, and without urgent intervention, over 220 more facilities could close by June.

a2391.speaker: Hajia Fatima Shinkafi, Executive Secretary of the Solid Minerals Development Fund (SMDF), in a statement signed by Mrs. Idowu Jokpeyibo, Head, Corporate Communications, SMDF
a2391.name: Hajia Fatima Shinkafi
a2391.title: Executive Secretary of the Solid Minerals Development Fund (SMDF), in a statement signed by Mrs. Idowu Jokpeyibo, Head, Corporate Communications, SMDF
a2391.speech: Emphasized the importance of diversifying Nigeria’s economy beyond crude oil by harnessing solid mineral resources ; praised the steadfast support of the Hon. Minister of Solid Minerals, Dr. Dele Alake, particularly his commitment to advancing women’s empowerment within the mining sector.

a2391.speaker: Hajia Fatima Shinkafi, Executive Secretary of the Solid Minerals Development Fund (SMDF)
a2391.name: Hajia Fatima Shinkafi
a2391.title: Executive Secretary of the Solid Minerals Development Fund (SMDF)
a2391.speech: “This training on gemstone and jewelry is not just about skill acquisition; it is a gateway to economic independence and social empowerment for Nigerian women,” Shinkafi said. She noted that the initiative would foster creativity, entrepreneurship, and resilience among participants, positioning them to build sustainable businesses in the gemstone industry.

a2391.speaker: Hajia Fatima Shinkafi, Executive Secretary of the Solid Minerals Development Fund (SMDF)
a2391.name: Hajia Fatima Shinkafi
a2391.title: Executive Secretary of the Solid Minerals Development Fund (SMDF)
a2391.speech: Confirmed that the program will offer loans and grants to help the women establish their own businesses. “We are focused not only on training but also on ensuring continuous growth for these women. The goal is to train 1,000 women, with opportunities for advanced training and support,” she added.

a2391.speaker: Engr. Janet Adeyemi, President of Nigeria Women in Mining
a2391.name: Engr. Janet Adeyemi
a2391.title: President of Nigeria Women in Mining
a2391.speech: Hailed the training program as a significant step in empowering women to participate in global mining and jewelry-making activities, and emphasized the importance of initiatives like this in making the mining sector more attractive to women and in raising women entrepreneurs.

a2391.speaker: Folakemi Akinleye, Nigeria’s former Ambassador to the Philippines and Cambodia
a2391.name: Folakemi Akinleye
a2391.title: Nigeria’s former Ambassador to the Philippines and Cambodia
a2391.speech: Stressed how similar programs in other countries have improved women’s economic contributions, and expressed confidence that the training would help overcome the barriers of inadequate skills and funding that have hindered women’s participation in the sector.

a2391.speaker: Participants at the event, including Sola Adesanya from Lagos, Eden Durosola Precious, and Hajia Umar Abubarkar from Zamfara
a2391.name: Participants at the event
a2391.title: including Sola Adesanya from Lagos, Eden Durosola Precious, and Hajia Umar Abubarkar from Zamfara
a2391.speech: Shared their optimism about the program’s potential to unlock new career opportunities in mining, and expressed gratitude to SMDF and Nigeria Women in Mining for giving them the platform to explore Nigeria’s mineral resources sustainably.

a2391.speaker: Dr. Tersoo Aga, geologist and program facilitator
a2391.name: Dr. Tersoo Aga
a2391.title: geologist and program facilitator
a2391.speech: Highlighted Nigeria’s abundance of over 500 types of gemstones and the vast potential for economic development in the solid minerals sector; emphasised that the pegmatite belt, which stretches across Nigeria, holds immense wealth that can be tapped into for sustainable economic growth.

a2435.speaker: Mohammed bin Abdulrahman, Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs of Qatar
a2435.name: Mohammed bin Abdulrahman
a2435.title: Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs of Qatar
a2435.speech: Announced on Wednesday evening the success of the mediators in concluding a ceasefire agreement in the Gaza Strip, noting that its implementation will begin this Sunday.

a2435.speaker: Ursula von der Leyen, President of the European Commission
a2435.name: Ursula von der Leyen
a2435.title: President of the European Commission
a2435.speech: Welcomed the ceasefire and the hostage agreement, declaring on X: “I warmly welcome the ceasefire and hostage release agreement in Gaza. The hostages will be reunited with their loved ones and humanitarian aid can reach civilians in Gaza. This brings hope to an entire region, where people have endured immense suffering for far too long. Both parties must fully implement this agreement, which constitutes a stepping stone towards lasting stability in the region and a diplomatic resolution of the conflict.”

a2435.speaker: Kaja Kallas, EU foreign policy chief
a2435.name: Kaja Kallas
a2435.title: EU foreign policy chief
a2435.speech: Expressed her support for the ceasefire, describing it as a significant breakthrough, declaring on X: “I welcome the ceasefire and hostage release agreement. This is a major and positive step towards ending the violence. It is now time to implement this agreement for all the hostages and their families, the people of Gaza and the people of the region.”

a2435.speaker: Roberta Metsola, President of the European Parliament
a2435.name: Roberta Metsola
a2435.title: President of the European Parliament
a2435.speech: Described the ceasefire and hostage release agreement as “the breakthrough the world was waiting for and that so many people needed,” adding: “It is essential that this ceasefire be respected. It can be a turning point towards lasting peace, an increase in aid and a catalyst that transforms despair into hope.”

a2435.speaker: Antonio Costa, President of the European Council
a2435.name: Antonio Costa
a2435.title: President of the European Council
a2435.speech: Welcomed the agreement, declaring: “I hope that this agreement will end the suffering of civilians and allow immediate access to the humanitarian aid they so badly need” ; reiterated the EU’s commitment to a “comprehensive, just and lasting peace based on the two-State solution.”

a2435.speaker: Keir Starmer, British Prime Minister
a2435.name: Keir Starmer
a2435.title: British Prime Minister
a2435.speech: Welcomed the ceasefire, calling it “the news long awaited by the Israeli and Palestinian peoples” ; stressed the need for aid and a path to peace: “This ceasefire must allow a considerable increase in humanitarian aid, which is so desperately needed to end the suffering in Gaza. And then, our attention must turn to how we ensure a lastingly better future for the Israeli and Palestinian peoples, based on a two-State solution that will guarantee Israel’s security and stability, alongside a sovereign and viable Palestinian State.”

a2435.speaker: Olaf Scholz, German Chancellor
a2435.name: Olaf Scholz
a2435.title: German Chancellor
a2435.speech: Said he was relieved by the ceasefire and hostage release agreement in Gaza, which includes German hostages: “The fact that an agreement on a ceasefire and the release of hostages in Gaza, including Germans, appears to have been concluded is good news! This agreement must now be applied to the letter. All hostages must be released” ; “This ceasefire opens the door to a definitive end to the war and to the improvement of the dire humanitarian situation in Gaza. We continue to work towards this.”

a2435.speaker: Emmanuel Macron, President of France
a2435.name: Emmanuel Macron
a2435.title: President of France
a2435.speech: Expressed his relief at the announcement, acknowledging the suffering of the people of Gaza: “After fifteen months of unjustifiable suffering, an immense relief for Gazans, a hope for the hostages and their families.”

a2435.speaker: Alexander De Croo, Belgian Prime Minister
a2435.name: Alexander De Croo
a2435.title: Belgian Prime Minister
a2435.speech: Expressed his relief, declaring: “After too many months of conflict, we feel immense relief for the hostages, for their families and for the people of Gaza. Let us hope that this ceasefire will end the fighting and mark the beginning of a lasting peace.”

a2435.speaker: Dick Schoof, Dutch Prime Minister
a2435.name: Dick Schoof
a2435.title: Dutch Prime Minister
a2435.speech: Welcomed the ceasefire as a “major step forward” and acknowledged the diplomatic efforts that made it possible, declaring on X: “The Netherlands strongly advocated for this outcome, in collaboration with its international partners. This agreement is an important step towards de-escalation in the Middle East and lasting peace.”

a2435.speaker: Jonas Gahr Støre, Norwegian Prime Minister
a2435.name: Jonas Gahr Støre
a2435.title: Norwegian Prime Minister
a2435.speech: Called the agreement “very encouraging and long awaited” and urged all parties to respect the terms, stressing that “weapons must be laid down, hostages released and sufficient humanitarian aid must reach Gaza” ; “The ceasefire is an important first step, but even if it holds, it will not bring lasting peace between Israelis and Palestinians. The conflict must now take a new direction. We need a political solution.”

a2435.speaker: Pedro Sánchez, Spanish Prime Minister
a2435.name: Pedro Sánchez
a2435.title: Spanish Prime Minister
a2435.speech: Stressed the importance of the agreement: “This agreement is crucial for achieving regional stability” ; “It represents an indispensable step towards the two-State solution and a peace respectful of international law.”

a2435.speaker: Annalena Baerbock, German Foreign Minister
a2435.name: Annalena Baerbock
a2435.title: German Foreign Minister
a2435.speech: Welcomed the ceasefire, stressing the hope for peace.

a2435.speaker: Caspar Veldkamp, Dutch Foreign Minister
a2435.name: Caspar Veldkamp
a2435.title: Dutch Foreign Minister
a2435.speech: Called the ceasefire a crucial step and stressed the need for it to be sustainable, declaring on X: “Positive news regarding a ceasefire in Gaza. It is now crucial that the agreement be respected and that hostilities cease, allowing the Israeli hostages to return home safely and ensuring that the people of Gaza receive the humanitarian aid they so urgently need.”

a2435.speaker: Micheál Martin, Irish Foreign Minister
a2435.name: Micheál Martin
a2435.title: Irish Foreign Minister
a2435.speech: Welcomed the agreement, stressing the immense suffering endured by civilians: “Far too many innocent people have been killed, in Gaza and in Israel, since the start of this conflict,” stressing the need for an increase in humanitarian aid and efforts to secure a two-State solution.

a2435.speaker: Bulgarian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a2435.name: Bulgarian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a2435.speech: Welcomed the ceasefire and hostage release agreement, declaring that Bulgaria “welcomes the tireless efforts of Egypt, Qatar and the United States.”

a2435.speaker: Save the Children UK (statement)
a2435.name: Save the Children UK (statement)
a2435.speech: Welcomed the ceasefire, emphasising its potential to protect children from further harm: “We are relieved that the Israeli government and Hamas have finally reached an agreement after 15 months of siege and bombardment by Israeli forces that followed the attacks by Palestinian armed groups in Israel on 7 October 2023.”

a2435.speaker: Cindy McCain, Executive Director of the World Food Programme
a2435.name: Cindy McCain
a2435.title: Executive Director of the World Food Programme
a2435.speech: Stressed the urgency of delivering humanitarian aid: “Promising news from Gaza” ; “@WFP has life-saving assistance ready at the borders to help feed more than one million Palestinians suffering from acute hunger, but we need: guaranteed security for humanitarian workers, safe movement of food through all border crossings and more funding to distribute at scale.”

a2435.speaker: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, Director-General of the WHO
a2435.name: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus
a2435.title: Director-General of the WHO
a2435.speech: Expressed the hope that the agreement would pave the way for lasting peace, declaring on X: “Too many lives have been lost and too many families have suffered” ; “Health needs in Gaza remain enormous. WHO is ready to scale up its support, alongside its partners.”

a2435.speaker: Jodie Ginsberg, Chief Executive of the Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ)
a2435.name: Jodie Ginsberg
a2435.title: Chief Executive of the Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ)
a2435.speech: Welcomed the agreement while expressing concern about the targeting of journalists during the conflict: “We call on the Egyptian, Palestinian and Israeli authorities to immediately allow foreign journalists to enter Gaza and on the international community to independently investigate the deliberate targeting of journalists.”

a2435.speaker: Agnès Callamard, Secretary General of Amnesty International
a2435.name: Agnès Callamard
a2435.title: Secretary General of Amnesty International
a2435.speech: Described the agreement as a “glimmer of relief” for Palestinians, but stressed that it was “cruelly overdue,” and that even with the cessation of fighting Palestinians still face dire living conditions: “For Palestinians, who have endured more than 15 months of devastating and relentless bombardment, who have been displaced from their homes repeatedly and who are struggling to survive in makeshift tents without food, water and basic necessities, the nightmare will not be over even if the bombs stop” ; condemned the Israeli blockade, urging the international community to ensure that humanitarian aid, particularly medical supplies, reaches Gaza.

a2476.speaker: Sources (anonymous, cited by Capital)
a2476.name: Sources (anonymous
a2476.title: cited by Capital)
a2476.speech: According to the information that Capital obtained from sources, the PM is expected to meet with an immense number of Ethiopian Diaspora in the near future ; according to sources, the Ethiopian embassy in Washington DC is working to gather thousands at the meeting with the PM.

a2476.speaker: EPRDF (ruling party)
a2476.name: EPRDF (ruling party)
a2476.speech: Announced the government would move to privatize some big enterprises.

a2476.speaker: Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed (PhD)
a2476.name: Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed (PhD)
a2476.speech: Has called for the Diaspora to be part of the change in the country, including outlawed opposition members that he has invited for discussions about political reforms.

a2476.speaker: Ethiopian opposition groups
a2476.name: Ethiopian opposition groups
a2476.speech: Some of the opposition groups have already announced that they have accepted his invitation and entered the country.

a2476.speaker: Ethiopian American LLC, organizer of the Ethiopian Diaspora Business Forum
a2476.name: Ethiopian American LLC
a2476.title: organizer of the Ethiopian Diaspora Business Forum
a2476.speech: Announced that the agendas of its latest event will focus on opening up investment sectors to the Diaspora; said that the 12th edition of the annual Ethiopian Diaspora Business Forum will this year focus on what roles the Diaspora may have in the future socio-economic landscape of the changing Ethiopia.

a2476.speaker: Organizers of the Ethiopian Diaspora Business Forum
a2476.name: Organizers of the Ethiopian Diaspora Business Forum
a2476.speech: According to the organizers, the theme of the forum is timely and critically important for the Ethiopian Diaspora community which is keen to chart out what positive roles to play in the fast changing Ethiopian landscape and the future of its economy and the community.

a2476.speaker: Yohannes Assefa, Executive Director of the Forum and Managing Director of Ethiopian American LLC
a2476.name: Yohannes Assefa
a2476.title: Executive Director of the Forum and Managing Director of Ethiopian American LLC
a2476.speech: "Ethiopia is at a crossroad in many ways. The recent economic reforms announced by the Government of Ethiopia will significantly change the way the Ethiopian Diaspora will invest and work in Ethiopia" ; said the Diaspora business community is eagerly awaiting to participate and support the process of liberalization in a thoughtful and prudent manner: "We are hopeful and encouraged by the proposed changes. We believe we can add value and contribute to the process while helping to avoid unintended challenges that could easily result from this process."

a2476.speaker: Ethiopian American LLC (statement sent to Capital)
a2476.name: Ethiopian American LLC (statement sent to Capital)
a2476.speech: Stated that a range of new investment policies have been tabled for discussion, including the opening of specific sectors in the past closed for Diaspora investment in Ethiopia: "The potential opening of the financial sector, media and telecom to Diaspora investments along with the ability of Diaspora professionals from the legal and other sectors to participate in Ethiopia's economy is monumental" ; said these changes will have huge impacts in the way the Diaspora will engage in Ethiopia's economy in the near future ; stated that Abiy is scheduled to travel to Washington to engage the Ethiopian Diaspora in the US during which he is also expected to announce a new approach of his administration in relation to Diaspora engagement.

a2476.speaker: Meles Alem, Spokesperson of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a2476.name: Meles Alem
a2476.title: Spokesperson of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a2476.speech: Told Capital that he does not have any information about the PM meeting with the Diaspora in the US.

a2514.speaker: Lucia Welwolie, 12th-grade student at Innovation Preparatory Academy International
a2514.name: Lucia Welwolie
a2514.title: 12th-grade student at Innovation Preparatory Academy International
a2514.speech: Delivered a speech highlighting the origins and significance of National Students Tax Day, emphasising the importance of empowering future leaders with taxation knowledge and its role in national development: "National Students Tax Day is a milestone in empowering us-the future leaders of Liberia-with the knowledge of taxation and its role in nation-building."

a2514.speaker: Lucia Welwolie, 12th-grade student at Innovation Preparatory Academy International
a2514.name: Lucia Welwolie
a2514.title: 12th-grade student at Innovation Preparatory Academy International
a2514.speech: Outlined the objectives of the Student Tax Education Program (STEP), which include promoting voluntary tax compliance and integrating tax education into Liberia's national civic curriculum, and urged stakeholders to ensure its full integration in Liberia's civic curriculum, calling on stakeholders to revisit a 2022 Memorandum of Understanding between the LRA, MoE, and WAEC Liberia to ensure the program's full implementation across all secondary schools; she proposed the establishment of National Students Tax Day as an annual event: "Let us rally behind the call to recognize National Students Tax Day as an annual working holiday."

a2514.speaker: Atty. Decontee T. King-Sackie, Managing Partner at ZE'AD Advisors and Consultants (keynote speaker)
a2514.name: Atty. Decontee T. King-Sackie
a2514.title: Managing Partner at ZE'AD Advisors and Consultants (keynote speaker)
a2514.speech: "When students are empowered through tax education, they transition seamlessly into adulthood as tax-compliant citizens, contributing to a diversified economy." ; referencing international models, she pointed out the successful enhancement of tax compliance and revenue generation in nations such as Finland, India, and South Africa through early educational initiatives, and recommended Liberia follow suit by incorporating tax education into academic programs and utilizing technology to facilitate learning ; "Tax education does more than create compliance. It nurtures informed, responsible citizens who fuel the engines of economic growth."

a2514.speaker: George Akl, Chief of Party for the USAID-LEAD Activity
a2514.name: George Akl
a2514.title: Chief of Party for the USAID-LEAD Activity
a2514.speech: Emphasized the societal importance of tax compliance: "Paying taxes is not just a legal obligation; it is a fundamental civic duty. It reflects your commitment to the common good and strengthens the social contract that unites us all."

a2514.speaker: Other partner institutions including the Ministry of Education
a2514.name: Other partner institutions including the Ministry of Education
a2514.speech: Praised the initiative and committed to supporting and integrating tax education into Liberia's development agenda.

a2530.speaker: Fitch Ratings (rating assessment)
a2530.name: Fitch Ratings (rating assessment)
a2530.speech: According to Fitch Ratings, the suspension of USAID support to Mozambique, which represented the equivalent to 3% of Mozambique's GDP, also impacted the country's foreign currency supply situation. "Foreign currency [FX] scarcity has increased in 2025, partly due to a decline in external disbursements to the government and the suspension of USAID (USD586 million in 2024, equivalent to 3% of GDP)," Fitch writes in its most recent rating assessment for the country.

a2530.speaker: Fitch Ratings (August assessment)
a2530.name: Fitch Ratings (August assessment)
a2530.speech: In its August assessment, which affirms Mozambique's CCC rating assigned in February, Fitch also admits that "the increase in April of the share of mandatory conversion of export receipts to local currency (to 50% from 30%)" will "ease some of the foreign exchange scarcity", as will the new program expected with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) by the end of the year ; Fitch also assesses Mozambique's reserves as "stable", but says "risks persist". It forecasts that Mozambique's international reserves will "remain broadly stable" in 2025, at US$3.5 billion.

a2530.speaker: Mozambican government (July data)
a2530.name: Mozambican government (July data)
a2530.speech: At least 2,500 jobs were lost in Mozambique due to the cut in USAID support, according to July data from the Mozambican government, which admitted it was "a problem" for the economy.

a2530.speaker: Ivete Alane, Mozambican Minister of Labour, Gender and Social Action
a2530.name: Ivete Alane
a2530.title: Mozambican Minister of Labour, Gender and Social Action
a2530.speech: "The last meeting I had with the group created by organizations that benefited from the funding spoke of around 2,500 jobs [lost]," she said recently, noting that there was no "official estimate".

a2530.speaker: Rogerio Zandamela, Governor of the Bank of Mozambique
a2530.name: Rogerio Zandamela
a2530.title: Governor of the Bank of Mozambique
a2530.speech: Said on July 31 that the Bank of Mozambique is adopting measures to increase "fluidity" in the foreign exchange market, attempting to redistribute the volume of available foreign exchange ; "These measures are nothing more than adjusting resources from here, taking them from here, putting them elsewhere, and better monitoring them." ; "An increase in fluidity in the foreign exchange market is expected. To boost sales to the public, the Bank of Mozambique recently reduced the daily retention limits for foreign exchange acquired by banks. This measure complements the decision to increase the minimum conversion rate for export revenues from 30% to 50%, which implies greater availability and access to foreign exchange." ; Responding to journalists regarding business owners' concerns about the lack of access to foreign exchange, particularly to guarantee imports, Zandamela admitted that "there was a need to adjust certain liquidity segments" ; "I repeat, this is very important. One thing is the aggregate distribution of liquidity, whether it exists as a whole in our system, and another is whether it is adequately distributed among the various segments of the country: among exporters, importers and investors."

a2530.speaker: Confederation of Economic Associations (CTA) of Mozambique
a2530.name: Confederation of Economic Associations (CTA) of Mozambique
a2530.speech: Warned on February 18 that the lack of foreign exchange in the banks' markets was affecting operations, especially in the healthcare, aviation, fuel, and food import sectors.

a2608.speaker: Investing in Innovation Africa (i3)
a2608.name: Investing in Innovation Africa (i3)
a2608.speech: Has decided to make a pivotal change to its 3rd cohort selection to prioritise the immediate support for 5-7 growth-stage companies building the Future of Pharmacy care in Africa; the i3 program will concentrate its immediate efforts to help innovative growth-stage startups unlock major partnerships to rapidly expand access to patient care, with selected start-ups receiving up to $225K in grant funds, and i3 aims to expand support to early-stage companies at a later date.

a2608.speaker: U.S. State Department (“stop-work” directive)
a2608.name: U.S. State Department (“stop-work” directive)
a2608.speech: Issued a “stop-work” directive for foreign aid on January 25th, which is anticipated to impact the distribution of essential medicine in Africa’s healthcare supply chains; the order highlights and intensifies the need for locally-driven, market-creating approaches to health product distribution and service delivery across Africa.

a2657.speaker: Professor Malcolm Shaw, counsel for the State of Israel before the International Court of Justice
a2657.name: Professor Malcolm Shaw
a2657.title: counsel for the State of Israel before the International Court of Justice
a2657.speech: Told the International Court of Justice that South Africa's case was misleading and should be rejected on the basis of law and precedent, while Israel's response to the 7 October attack by Hamas did not constitute genocide. On context: "the immediate and proximate context for the specific allegations of genocide claimed by South Africa lies in the events of 7 October, when Hamas militants and other armed groups and individuals stormed into the internationally recognized sovereign territory of Israel and committed acts of barely credible atrocity... Indeed, such acts may be seen as the real genocide in this situation." ; "Armed conflict, even when fully justified and conducted lawfully, is brutal and costs lives... Not every conflict is genocidal... if claims of genocide were to become the common currency of armed conflict, whenever and wherever that occurred, the essence of this crime would be diluted and lost."

a2657.speaker: Professor Malcolm Shaw, counsel for the State of Israel
a2657.name: Professor Malcolm Shaw
a2657.title: counsel for the State of Israel
a2657.speech: On prima facie jurisdiction and the existence of a dispute: argued that "Unilateral assertion does not suffice. There needs to be some element of engagement between the parties... A dispute is a reciprocal phenomenon." Said South Africa "cites no relevant exchange between the Parties" and that "There is no evidence of 'positive opposition' as required by the Court"; "This is not a dispute, it is a 'unispute' - a one-sided clapping of hands." Argued South Africa's Application incorrectly stated Israel had not responded to its Note Verbale, that Israel responded that very day and repeatedly offered meetings, and that "South Africa did not give Israel a reasonable opportunity to engage with it on the matters under consideration before filing its no doubt long-prepared Application."

a2657.speaker: Professor Malcolm Shaw, counsel for the State of Israel
a2657.name: Professor Malcolm Shaw
a2657.title: counsel for the State of Israel
a2657.speech: On intent: "What determines the existence of the crime of genocide is the intention to destroy, in whole or in part, a particular group, as such... To consider the acts alone as listed in Article II, with no reference at all to the intent criterion, is thus to denude the crime of its very essence: Hamlet without the Prince; a car without an engine." ; "there is little beyond random assertions to demonstrate that Israel has or has had the specific intent to destroy, in whole or in part, the Palestinian people, as such." ; Argued that Israel's targeting practices, mitigation of civilian harm and facilitation of humanitarian assistance "all demonstrate the precise opposite of any possible genocidal intent", and that South Africa "presents a distorted picture" and "misunderstands the nature and provenance of certain comments made by some Israeli politicians"; to produce random quotes not in conformity with government policy "is described as misleading at best".

a2657.speaker: Professor Malcolm Shaw, counsel for the State of Israel
a2657.name: Professor Malcolm Shaw
a2657.title: counsel for the State of Israel
a2657.speech: On plausibility and the rights to be protected: "plausibility is an elusive concept. Simply declaring that claimed rights are plausible is insufficient." ; Said "Provisional measures are intended to constitute a shield and not a sword. To preserve not undermine rights", and that "the Court needs to consider the relevant respective rights of both Parties, Respondent as well as the Applicant", chief among them Israel's inherent right of self-defence.

a2657.speaker: Professor Malcolm Shaw, counsel for the State of Israel
a2657.name: Professor Malcolm Shaw
a2657.title: counsel for the State of Israel
a2657.speech: On Hamas and South Africa's role: "if there has been any genocidal activity in this situation, it was the events of 7 October"; argued that States "that supported, condoned, praised or glorified the events of 7 October... stand guilty of a violation of Article III (e) of the Convention as being complicit in genocide" and that "South Africa has given succour and support to Hamas. At the least."

a2657.speaker: Professor Malcolm Shaw, counsel for the State of Israel
a2657.name: Professor Malcolm Shaw
a2657.title: counsel for the State of Israel
a2657.speech: Conclusion: "Allegations have been made which verge on the outrageous. The attack by Hamas on 7 October, with its deliberate commission of atrocities, clearly falls within the statutory definition of genocide. Israel's response was and remains legitimate and necessary... There is no genocidal intent here. This is no genocide." ; "South Africa tells us only half the story."

a2657.speaker: South Africa's Application to the International Court of Justice
a2657.name: South Africa's Application to the International Court of Justice
a2657.speech: Declares that "it is important to place the acts of genocide in the broader context of Israel's conduct towards [the] Palestinians during its 75-year-long apartheid". The Application further states that "Israel has not responded directly to South Africa's Note Verbale"; it also stated that "the dispute is plainly not capable of resolution by way of a bilateral meeting".

a2657.speaker: President of the European Commission
a2657.name: President of the European Commission
a2657.speech: As the President of the European Commission put it on 19 October: "There was no limit to the blood Hamas terrorists wanted to spill. They went home by home. They burned people alive. They mutilated children and even babies. Why? Because they were Jews. Because they were living in the State of Israel. And Hamas' explicit goal is to eradicate Jewish life from the Holy Land. These terrorists, supported by their friends in Tehran, will never stop. And so, Israel has the right to defend itself in line with humanitarian law."

a2657.speaker: International Court of Justice (case law and orders cited)
a2657.name: International Court of Justice (case law and orders cited)
a2657.speech: Emphasised in its Order of 2 June 1999 that the threat or use of force cannot in itself constitute an act of genocide within the meaning of Article II of the Genocide Convention; reaffirmed in the Myanmar case that "[i]t must be shown that the claim of one party is positively opposed by the other" and that "the function of provisional measures... is to protect the respective rights of either party pending its final decision"; referred in the Marshall Islands cases to the need that the Respondent should not "be deprived of the opportunity to react before the institution of proceedings"; made clear that "claims against a State involving charges of exceptional gravity must be proved by evidence that is fully conclusive"; and in its Order of 16 March 2022 in Ukraine v. Russia stated that the power to indicate provisional measures "has as its object the preservation of the respective rights claimed by the parties in a case, pending its decision on the merits thereof."

a2657.speaker: Professor John Dugard, counsel for South Africa
a2657.name: Professor John Dugard
a2657.title: counsel for South Africa
a2657.speech: Explains that South Africa had voiced its concerns in the Security Council and in public statements, and had further referred the matter to the International Criminal Court; at that point, he says, it became clear there was a serious dispute between the two States. Concludes that "Israel must have been aware from South Africa's public statements, d[é]marche and referral to the International Criminal Court of Israel's genocidal acts that a dispute existed between the two States", and declares that "special considerations" apply to the existence of disputes concerning Article IX of the Genocide Convention.

a2657.speaker: Judge Greenwood (in the Border Area case)
a2657.name: Judge Greenwood (in the Border Area case)
a2657.speech: Emphasised that "[w]hat is required is something more than assertion but less than proof; in other words, the party must show that there is at least a reasonable possibility that the right it claims exists as a matter of law and will be adjudged to apply to that party's case."

a2657.speaker: Judge Tomka
a2657.name: Judge Tomka
a2657.speech: Has noted that sometimes statements are made which are "nothing more than a part of the recent war-time rhetoric intending to put the blame and shame on the other side".

a2657.speaker: Benjamin Netanyahu, Prime Minister of Israel
a2657.name: Benjamin Netanyahu
a2657.title: Prime Minister of Israel
a2657.speech: Publicly declared on 28 October that "the IDF is doing everything possible to avoid harming those not involved", and on 18 November declared that "first of all, and above all else, Israel acts according to the laws of war. This is how our army works." ; On 10 January: "Israel has no intention of permanently occupying Gaza or displacing its civilian population. Israel is fighting Hamas terrorists, not the Palestinian population, and we are doing so in full compliance with international law. The IDF is doing its utmost to minimize civilian casualties, while Hamas is doing its utmost to maximize them by using Palestinian civilians as human shields... Our goal is to rid Gaza of Hamas terrorists and free our hostages." ; On 23 November: "Any civilian death is a tragedy. Any one. And to avoid them, what you do is first, you try to get the civilians out of harm's way. And that's exactly what we did." ; Statement of 28 October: "We are now entering the second phase of the war, which its objectives are clear: destruction of the military and governmental capabilities of Hamas and the return of the hostages back home... Remember what Amalek has done to you. We remember, and we are fighting... The IDF is the most moral army in the world, the IDF does everything to avoid harming the uninvolved..."

a2657.speaker: Israeli Ministerial Committee on National Security Affairs, 29 October (internal cabinet decisions, tab 1A)
a2657.name: Israeli Ministerial Committee on National Security Affairs
a2657.title: 29 October (internal cabinet decisions, tab 1A)
