a2657.speech: Instructions from the Prime Minister stating: (i) "The Prime Minister stated time and again . . . we must prevent a humanitarian disaster"; (ii) "The Prime Minister indicated the possible sorts of solutions that will ensure required supply of water, food and medicine: increasing the amount of trucks entering, [with] the necessary inspections"; (iii) "[P]romoting the construction of field hospitals in the south of the Gaza Strip".

a2657.speaker: Minister of Defence of Israel
a2657.name: Minister of Defence of Israel
a2657.speech: Publicly stated on 29 October that "we are not fighting the Palestinian multitude and the Palestinian people in Gaza" and declared on 13 November that "[o]ur war is against the Hamas terrorist organization, not the people of Gaza".

a2657.speaker: President of Israel
a2657.name: President of Israel
a2657.speech: Declared on 12 October that "we are working, operating militarily according to rules of international law. Period. Unequivocally."

a2657.speaker: Operations Directorate of the Israel Defense Forces (daily operational directive, tab 1B)
a2657.name: Operations Directorate of the Israel Defense Forces (daily operational directive
a2657.title: tab 1B)
a2657.speech: Stating that "[a]ttacks will be solely directed towards military targets, while adhering to the principles of distinction, proportionality and the obligation taking precautions in attacks in order to reduce collateral damage"; that "the laws of armed conflict allow destruction to civilian property only when there is a military necessity to do so, and prohibit harm to property for deterrence purposes only or for the purpose of punishment (individual or collective)"; and that it "is necessary to treat enemy civilians with respect, they should not be treated in a humiliating manner and civilians should not be used for the purpose of performing activities that might put them under risk to their life or their body".

a2657.speaker: Professor Vaughan Lowe, counsel for South Africa
a2657.name: Professor Vaughan Lowe
a2657.title: counsel for South Africa
a2657.speech: Sought to maintain yesterday that Israel has no right to self-defence in this situation.

a2885.speaker: Source close to Hezbollah (anonymous)
a2885.name: Source close to Hezbollah (anonymous)
a2885.speech: Said the head of Hezbollah's feared security apparatus was the target of the Israeli air strikes carried out on Thursday on Beirut ; the raid targeted "the head of Hezbollah's security apparatus Wafic Safa", a source close to the pro-Iranian movement told AFP, without further information on his fate ; according to the source close to Hezbollah, this shows that Israel "has moved to a new stage, by targeting the political officials" of the movement.

a2885.speaker: Lebanese Health Ministry
a2885.name: Lebanese Health Ministry
a2885.speech: According to the Health Ministry, the strikes left 22 dead and 117 wounded.

a2885.speaker: Bilal Othman, resident of Basta, Beirut
a2885.name: Bilal Othman
a2885.title: resident of Basta, Beirut
a2885.speech: "Many families live here," he fumed, amid heaps of concrete and twisted iron. "Why did they (the Israelis) target" the area, "do they want to tell us that there is no longer any safe place in the country?"

a2885.speaker: Antony Blinken, US Secretary of State
a2885.name: Antony Blinken
a2885.title: US Secretary of State
a2885.speech: Declared on Friday that the United States supports the efforts made by Lebanon to "assert itself" in the face of Hezbollah ; said on Friday that the United States still hoped to prevent "a wider conflict" in the Middle East.

a2885.speaker: Antony Blinken, US Secretary of State
a2885.name: Antony Blinken
a2885.title: US Secretary of State
a2885.speech: The United States has conveyed to its Israeli ally its "real concerns" about the lack of humanitarian aid in the sector [Gaza], according to Mr Blinken.

a2885.speaker: Benjamin Netanyahu, Israeli Prime Minister
a2885.name: Benjamin Netanyahu
a2885.title: Israeli Prime Minister
a2885.speech: On Tuesday had called on the neighbouring country to "free itself" from Hezbollah, on pain of suffering the same fate as Gaza.

a2885.speaker: Lebanon (government)
a2885.name: Lebanon (government)
a2885.speech: On Friday, denounced new Israeli fire on a position of the Blue Helmets in southern Lebanon.

a2885.speaker: Antonio Guterres, UN Secretary-General
a2885.name: Antonio Guterres
a2885.title: UN Secretary-General
a2885.speech: Castigated on Friday that Israeli fire against the Blue Helmets constitutes "a violation of international humanitarian law".

a2885.speaker: Israeli army
a2885.name: Israeli army
a2885.speech: Said it had fired on Thursday "next to" UNIFIL headquarters, insisting it had warned its personnel to take cover.

a2885.speaker: AFP count based on official figures
a2885.name: AFP count based on official figures
a2885.speech: Since October 2023, more than 2,000 people have been killed in Lebanon, including nearly 1,200 since 23 September, according to an AFP count based on official figures ; the war in Gaza was triggered on 7 October 2023 by the Hamas attack on Israel which led to the deaths of 1,206 people, mostly civilians, according to an AFP count based on official Israeli figures.

a2885.speaker: United Nations (UN)
a2885.name: United Nations (UN)
a2885.speech: The UN has put at 600,000 the number of people displaced inside Lebanon ; at least 400,000 people are caught in a vice in the zone [Jabalia], according to the UN.

a2885.speaker: Hezbollah
a2885.name: Hezbollah
a2885.speech: Says it is resisting the Israeli army, and is continuing its fire against the country. On Friday, it announced that it had "launched a squadron of attack drones on an air base in Haifa" in northern Israel.

a2885.speaker: Israeli rescue services
a2885.name: Israeli rescue services
a2885.speech: Announced that a Thai agricultural worker had been killed by an anti-tank missile in northern Israel, with the army reporting two civilians wounded.

a2885.speaker: Yoav Gallant, Israeli Defence Minister
a2885.name: Yoav Gallant
a2885.title: Israeli Defence Minister
a2885.speech: Israel is preparing, according to its Defence Minister Yoav Gallant, a "deadly, precise and surprising" response to the missile attack launched by Tehran against Israeli territory on 1 October.

a2885.speaker: Iran
a2885.name: Iran
a2885.speech: Reaffirmed on Friday that it was ready to "defend its sovereignty" against Israel, which it says it struck to avenge the assassination in Tehran of the Hamas leader, as well as those of the Lebanese Hezbollah leader and of a general of the Iranian Revolutionary Guards.

a2885.speaker: Mahmoud Bassal, spokesman for Gaza's Civil Defence
a2885.name: Mahmoud Bassal
a2885.title: spokesman for Gaza's Civil Defence
a2885.speech: According to Mahmoud Bassal, at least 140 people have died in Jabalia since the start of the operation.

a2885.speaker: Palestinian Red Crescent
a2885.name: Palestinian Red Crescent
a2885.speech: On Thursday, 28 Gazans were killed in an Israeli strike on a school in Deir el-Balah (centre) sheltering displaced people, according to the Palestinian Red Crescent.

a2885.speaker: Israeli army
a2885.name: Israeli army
a2885.speech: Spoke of a "precise" air strike on "terrorists".

a2885.speaker: Health Ministry of the Hamas government
a2885.name: Health Ministry of the Hamas government
a2885.speech: At least 42,065 Palestinians have been killed, mostly civilians, in the Israeli offensive in Gaza, according to data from the Health Ministry of the Hamas government, considered reliable by the UN.

a2982.speaker: Mastercard, Alerzo and the USAID-funded e-Trade Alliance (the firms)
a2982.name: Mastercard
a2982.title: Alerzo and the USAID-funded e-Trade Alliance (the firms)
a2982.speech: According to the firms, this collaboration will be reached by the end of the year.

a2982.speaker: Folasade Femi-Lawal, Country Manager, West Africa, Mastercard
a2982.name: Folasade Femi-Lawal
a2982.title: Country Manager, West Africa, Mastercard
a2982.speech: "Mastercard is committed to driving financial inclusion and empowering small businesses worldwide. Our collaboration with Alerzo and the e-Trade Alliance in Nigeria provides MSMEs the digital tools and resources needed to thrive in today's digital economy." ; "By facilitating seamless digital payments and offering comprehensive business management solutions, we are fostering a more inclusive financial ecosystem and driving innovation and growth within the sector. This collaboration demonstrates the immense possibilities that can be unlocked through the power of public-private partnerships."

a3011.speaker: Adama Kinda, President of the Centre-Nord Regional Chamber of Agriculture (CRA/CN)
a3011.name: Adama Kinda
a3011.title: President of the Centre-Nord Regional Chamber of Agriculture (CRA/CN)
a3011.speech: Said that 340 livestock keepers, spread across 170 tents, from the three provinces of the Centre-Nord region (Sanmatenga, Bam and Namentenga) took part in the event with more than 3,700 small ruminants and 2,200 poultry. “The prices of small ruminants range between 50,000 and 125,000 CFA francs” ; Said the objective is not only to promote local products but also to forge relationships between herders and buyers.

a3011.speaker: Sommanogo Koutou, Minister of Animal and Fisheries Resources (MRAH)
a3011.name: Sommanogo Koutou
a3011.title: Minister of Animal and Fisheries Resources (MRAH)
a3011.speech: Stressed that this initiative makes it possible to establish a win-win partnership between the various actors in the livestock sector for better marketing of the products of the small ruminant and poultry value chains. “It is also an opportunity to consolidate the ties already forged during previous editions” ; Expressed his gratitude to USAID for its support in the continued organisation of this event ; “The fair is part of strengthening the resilience of vulnerable communities, which lies at the heart of national priorities.”

a3011.speaker: Sommanogo Koutou, Minister of Animal and Fisheries Resources (MRAH)
a3011.name: Sommanogo Koutou
a3011.title: Minister of Animal and Fisheries Resources (MRAH)
a3011.speech: Said that in Burkina Faso livestock farming, practised by more than 80% of the population, contributes more than 18% of GDP and represents nearly 26% of exports by value.

a3011.speaker: Sibidou Kaboré, member of the Tégawendé cooperative from Boulsa
a3011.name: Sibidou Kaboré
a3011.title: member of the Tégawendé cooperative from Boulsa
a3011.speech: “This fair allows us to sell our products. For example, at the previous edition, we sold more than 50 sheep for receipts of more than 4.5 million CFA francs.”

a3040.speaker: European Commission (leaked proposal for the next long-term budget cycle)
a3040.name: European Commission (leaked proposal for the next long-term budget cycle)
a3040.speech: calls for conditioning development aid for African countries on meeting migration-reduction targets.

a3040.speaker: Amnesty International
a3040.name: Amnesty International
a3040.speech: According to Amnesty International, the EU's externalisation policy, coupled with Italy and Malta's hostility to rescue ships, was responsible for 721 migrant deaths in the Mediterranean between June and July 2018.

a3040.speaker: Several European rescue organisations
a3040.name: Several European rescue organisations
a3040.speech: blamed the deaths of 3,000 people in the Mediterranean in 2023 partly on an EU decree enacted that year that severely restricted their response capacity.

a3040.speaker: African governments
a3040.name: African governments
a3040.speech: largely oppose the EU's forced return of migrants, for both humanitarian and economic reasons ; are also quick to note that they bear the brunt of African migration. Of the more than 45 million people forcibly displaced in Africa last year, 34.5 million remained within their own countries.

a3040.speaker: European Court of Auditors
a3040.name: European Court of Auditors
a3040.speech: In 2024, the European Court of Auditors criticised the bloc's five billion euro Emergency Trust Fund for Africa for failing to address the human-rights risks involved in subcontracting migration policy to autocratic regimes in Tunisia, Egypt, and Libya.

a3040.speaker: European External Action Service (leaked internal report)
a3040.name: European External Action Service (leaked internal report)
a3040.speech: warned that continued support for Tunisia, which has cracked down hard on dissent, would damage the EU's reputation.

a3040.speaker: United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), 2019 report
a3040.name: United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)
a3040.title: 2019 report
a3040.speech: A 2019 report by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), based on interviews with 1,970 African migrants from 39 countries, conducted across 13 EU member states, found that they were typically educated above the average levels in their home countries and had held steady jobs there. But only 38pc said they had earned enough "to get by."

a3180.speaker: U.S. Department of State (statement)
a3180.name: U.S. Department of State (statement)
a3180.speech: According to a statement released by the U.S. Department of State, the Joint Oversight Committee - comprising representatives from both the DRC and Rwanda - is tasked with monitoring implementation, resolving disputes, and addressing violations of the agreement; the parties adopted terms of reference, named their committee chairpersons, and discussed mechanisms for future meetings ; The statement emphasized that both Rwanda and the DRC "expressed their appreciation for the invaluable contributions and joint efforts" of these partners.

a3180.speaker: William Ruto, Kenyan President (statement posted on X, formerly Twitter)
a3180.name: William Ruto
a3180.title: Kenyan President (statement posted on X, formerly Twitter)
a3180.speech: Said the East African Community (EAC) and the Southern African Development Community (SADC) remain fully engaged in efforts to end the conflict and prevent further humanitarian crises ; "Our resolve to end war, loss of life and ensure comprehensive humanitarian assistance in the DRC made a leap forward," highlighting the appointment of five facilitators by the two regional blocs.

a3239.speaker: United Nations
a3239.name: United Nations
a3239.speech: According to the United Nations, at least 117 million people will not receive food or other humanitarian assistance in 2025 due to funding shortfalls; the organisation estimates that 307 million people will require aid next year, but current funding levels only allow assistance for about 60% of them.

a3239.speaker: Tom Fletcher, U.N. under-secretary-general for humanitarian affairs
a3239.name: Tom Fletcher
a3239.title: U.N. under-secretary-general for humanitarian affairs
a3239.speech: "We have been forced to scale back appeals to those in most dire need."

a3239.speaker: Rania Dagash-Kamara, World Food Program (WFP)
a3239.name: Rania Dagash-Kamara
a3239.title: World Food Program (WFP)
a3239.speech: Described the stark reality in Syria, where aid has been drastically reduced: "We are at this point taking from the hungry to feed the starving."

a3239.speaker: Jan Egeland, head of the Norwegian Refugee Council
a3239.name: Jan Egeland
a3239.title: head of the Norwegian Refugee Council
a3239.speech: "How come there is not more interest in helping starving children in the rest of the world?"

a3239.speaker: Julia Steets, director of the Global Public Policy Institute
a3239.name: Julia Steets
a3239.title: director of the Global Public Policy Institute
a3239.speech: "Aid tends to arrive when the animals are dead, people are on the move, and children are malnourished."

a3239.speaker: A U.S. official (anonymous)
a3239.name: A U.S. official (anonymous)
a3239.speech: Defended funding restrictions, saying they are necessary "to ensure the responsible use of U.S. taxpayer funds."

a3239.speaker: Martin Griffiths, former U.N. relief chief
a3239.name: Martin Griffiths
a3239.title: former U.N. relief chief
a3239.speech: Called for a change in the funding model, suggesting a mandatory fee system for member states.

a3239.speaker: Jens Laerke, U.N. spokesperson
a3239.name: Jens Laerke
a3239.title: U.N. spokesperson
a3239.speech: "We can't just rely on the same club of donors," urging a more diversified donor base to address the growing crisis.

a3275.speaker: Colombe J. H. Doyigbe, Director of Human Resources in charge of Volunteering at the National Agency for Employment (AnpE) of Benin
a3275.name: Colombe J. H. Doyigbe
a3275.title: Director of Human Resources in charge of Volunteering at the National Agency for Employment (AnpE) of Benin
a3275.speech: "Volunteering, which is a driver of development, refers to the act of committing oneself on a voluntary basis to activities of general interest, without expecting financial remuneration." ; said volunteers offer their time, their skills, and sometimes their resources, to support varied causes such as humanitarian aid, protection of the environment, education, health and community development; indicated that although it is an altruistic act, it allows one to flourish and is governed by ethical principles and rules, citing respect, human dignity, solidarity, non-harm, responsibility and dedication; instructed the young people on the rights and duties of the volunteer; and cited the volunteering programmes: Exchange and Mobility Volunteering (International Reciprocity Volunteering), the Talents Africains a l'International (TAI) project and the Programme to Support the Development of National Volunteering Ecosystems in Africa (DENVA).

a3275.speaker: Raymonde Lao, Head of the AnpE departmental branch (Alibori, Kandi)
a3275.name: Raymonde Lao
a3275.title: Head of the AnpE departmental branch (Alibori, Kandi)
a3275.speech: Urged the young people to follow the session attentively and spoke to them about the advantage of volunteering linked to professional integration, saying that volunteering makes it possible to strengthen employability by offering practical experience, the development of specific skills and the possibility of building a professional network, thus facilitating entry into the labour market.

a3275.speaker: Salmane Babamoussa, Employment Adviser at the AnpE
a3275.name: Salmane Babamoussa
a3275.title: Employment Adviser at the AnpE
a3275.speech: Lifted a corner of the veil on everything being implemented by the Government through the National Agency for Employment to promote the professional integration of young people, and presented to the audience the core business of the Agency, which is intermediation between supply and demand, as well as the various projects and programmes of the AnpE put in place by the Government, including the Support Programme for Self-Employment, the Decentralised Partnership for Employment, PAPCO, P2RDE, the Youth Inclusion Project (ProDIJ) from which the Azoli scheme stems, the Special Programme for Integration into Employment (PSIE) and the Special Programme for Pre-Integration into Teaching (PSPIE).

a3294.speaker: Thomas Nyarko Ampem, Deputy Minister of Finance designate of Ghana
a3294.name: Thomas Nyarko Ampem
a3294.title: Deputy Minister of Finance designate of Ghana
a3294.speech: Has said that the 10 per cent increase in the base pay for workers in the country will lead to more than GH¢11 billion increase in compensation bills. He said the percentage increment was appropriate under the current economic circumstances, adding that the government was willing to give more to workers when the situation got better: “We are happy; we are grateful to the labour unions for this understanding. I believe that when the economy picks up, we would be in a position to do more for labour.”

a3294.speaker: Frank Annor Dompreh, Minority Chief Whip
a3294.name: Frank Annor Dompreh
a3294.title: Minority Chief Whip
a3294.speech: Asked whether he found the 10 per cent given to labour acceptable, as compared to the 30 plus per cent given by the previous government or not.

a3294.speaker: Thomas Nyarko Ampem, Deputy Minister of Finance designate of Ghana
a3294.name: Thomas Nyarko Ampem
a3294.title: Deputy Minister of Finance designate of Ghana
a3294.speech: Described the various stakeholder forums being organised by the government to brainstorm as necessary for consensus building: “This is intended to build consensus on the way forward. President Mahama is focused on delivery, but it is always important to carry people along.” The nominee expressed the hope that “unlike the Senchi consensus, our brothers and sisters on the other side will participate in this one so we all put our hands together to build a better Ghana, to reset Ghana”.

a3294.speaker: Jerry Ahmed Shaib, Member of Parliament for Weija Gbawe
a3294.name: Jerry Ahmed Shaib
a3294.title: Member of Parliament for Weija Gbawe
a3294.speech: Asked a question about the stakeholder forums being organised by the government.

a3294.speaker: Thomas Nyarko Ampem, Deputy Minister of Finance designate of Ghana
a3294.name: Thomas Nyarko Ampem
a3294.title: Deputy Minister of Finance designate of Ghana
a3294.speech: Answering a question on the decision of the US government to withdraw its USAID programme, said that President Mahama had instructed the Finance Minister to look for funding to support programmes that might be affected by the withdrawal: “We know that aid to our country has been dwindling over the years. DANIDA is no longer supporting programmes in Ghana as it used to. The United Kingdom, for instance, has reduced their aid budget from 0.75 per cent of GNP to 0.5 per cent. This should tell us that it will get to a time aid to our country will probably dwindle to zero. The only difference between the need for donor funding and that of the USAID is that the announcement about USAID withdrawal came suddenly, but we have seen the trend that aid is dwindling and so it is important that we begin to plan our lives without aid and see what we can do for ourselves.”

a3307.speaker: Ministry of Health statistics (Tanzania)
a3307.name: Ministry of Health statistics (Tanzania)
a3307.speech: Show that a total of 23,850 people living with HIV arrived at health service facilities in the country already in the advanced stages of HIV and AIDS over the six-month period from July to December 2024; of those tested, 14,051 were in the third and fourth stage of the disease, while 9,804 had a CD4 cell count below 200.

a3307.speaker: Dr Sylvester Kwilasa, Programme Officer, National AIDS, Sexually Transmitted Infections and Hepatitis Control Programme (NASHCoP)
a3307.name: Dr Sylvester Kwilasa
a3307.title: Programme Officer, National AIDS, Sexually Transmitted Infections and Hepatitis Control Programme (NASHCoP)
a3307.speech: "Within this number, 47,212 PLHIV were tested for CD4 and 34,508 PLHIV were assessed by HIV WHO Clinical Staging. Of these, 9,804 PLHIV had CD4 below 200 and 14,051 PLHIV were at HIV WHO Clinical Staging stages 3 and 4. Thus, the number of PLHIV who had AHD in this period is 23,850." ; "These are statistics obtained through the HIV Care and Treatment Services Unit (CTC)" ; said the ministry has been ensuring there is follow-up of AHD patients after treatment through the CTC system.

a3307.speaker: Dr Sylvester Kwilasa, Programme Officer, NASHCoP
a3307.name: Dr Sylvester Kwilasa
a3307.title: Programme Officer, NASHCoP
a3307.speech: Speaking about the availability of treatment, said those found at advanced stages have been given special medicines available at all health facilities: "Medicines for Cryptococcus infection and tuberculosis are available at public hospitals and health centres. In addition, medicines for Cryptococcal meningitis are available at hospitals that are recognised and have the capacity to provide those services" ; said the Government has ensured the availability of Cotrimoxazole and anti-TB medicines (3HR, 3HP, INH) together with the provision of preventive treatment (prophylaxis) at public hospitals and health centres ; "These services are available at all facilities providing care and treatment services (CTC) through a special system. In addition, the Government has a plan to increase AHD centres up to the level of district hospitals across the whole country by March 2025" ; said NASHCoP has been taking various measures to ensure emergency services are available to that group, including ensuring the availability of CD4 reagents and reagents for testing opportunistic illnesses; said the Ministry of Health has been monitoring implementation of the AHD intervention through implementation reports.

a3307.speaker: Dr Sylvester Kwilasa, Programme Officer, NASHCoP
a3307.name: Dr Sylvester Kwilasa
a3307.title: Programme Officer, NASHCoP
a3307.speech: On funding and collaboration, said: "The Government has been collaborating with international organisations such as WHO, PEPFAR and the Global Fund in fighting and providing AHD services through various means such as funding the purchase of reagents and medicines, supporting the development of guidelines and helping to train service providers." ; "International organisations, through development partners in collaboration with the Government, have been overseeing the provision of AHD services at public hospitals and health centres."

a3307.speaker: Dr Joshua Kajula, Coordinator of the HIV Care and Treatment Services Unit (CTC), Amana Regional Referral Hospital
a3307.name: Dr Joshua Kajula
a3307.title: Coordinator of the HIV Care and Treatment Services Unit (CTC), Amana Regional Referral Hospital
a3307.speech: Said the problem affects some young people; said that between 2023 and 2024, of the 390 patients who started services at that unit and were found to have Advanced HIV Disease, 170 were adults, 42 were children under 24, while 12 patients had the disease ; "Many feel that they are infected, but they are afraid to get tested to know their health status. A person is sick but is afraid to go and be tested, so he finds himself taking a different path. Another one will go round to every kind of traditional healer, is treated at a pharmacy by buying medicines, and others go to religious faiths, to various prophets. When they see it has failed, a relative brings them in. By the time he arrives at the hospital he is helpless, and that is when we begin to treat him and see how to raise his CD4 count."

a3307.speaker: Dr Kija Kibwana, Chalinze Hospital
a3307.name: Dr Kija Kibwana
a3307.title: Chalinze Hospital
a3307.speech: Said that in 2024 that council identified three patients who had AHD, who have already started taking medication ; "If a service recipient is continuing with treatment, at the start we test their CD4. If the test shows above 350, they should not have to take that test again after every short interval. But if the results are below that level, they will be tested every six months to monitor their immunity" ; said they are serving 128 young people aged 15-24 at that facility, of whom 48 are male and 80 are female.

a3307.speaker: Health experts
a3307.name: Health experts
a3307.speech: Have said that the number of people living with HIV who have reached the advanced stage of the disease shows that there is no awareness about testing for HIV infection within the community, a situation that endangers public health and raises the prospect of resistance to antiretroviral (ARV) drugs among people living with HIV.

a3307.speaker: Dr Mugisha Nkoronko, President of the Medical Association of Tanzania (MAT)
a3307.name: Dr Mugisha Nkoronko
a3307.title: President of the Medical Association of Tanzania (MAT)
a3307.speech: "These advanced stages contribute to more infections, because a person living with HIV who reaches the third and fourth stage of the disease without having found out is likely to infect others." ; "It also indicates the existence of stigma, failure to take medication consistently, and the distance to reach health services."

a3307.speaker: Study carried out in rural areas of Tanzania
a3307.name: Study carried out in rural areas of Tanzania
a3307.speech: Showed that, despite implementation of the World Health Organization (WHO) Test and Treat guidelines, there is still a large burden of AHD and of deaths associated with that condition.

a3307.speaker: Research/studies
a3307.name: Research/studies
a3307.speech: Have shown that 42.4 percent of people diagnosed with HIV in Tanzania are diagnosed when already at a late stage, and 17.7 percent when at the AHD stage, with approximately 60,000 new infections each year among people aged 15 and above.

a3417.speaker: Le Monde (leading French newspaper)
a3417.name: Le Monde (leading French newspaper)
a3417.speech: Denounced on Wednesday the "disguised expulsion" of its Moscow correspondent Benjamin Quenelle after his press accreditation was revoked, saying that after four months of suspension Quenelle's press card was "cancelled" by the Russian authorities.

a3417.speaker: Jerome Fenoglio, Le Monde's editorial director
a3417.name: Jerome Fenoglio
a3417.title: Le Monde's editorial director
a3417.speech: "This revocation of our right to practice our profession is without precedent." ; "This arbitrary decision constitutes a new obstacle to the freedom of the press in the country." ; "Even in the tensest moments of the Cold War, Le Monde pursued its work in Moscow and beyond."

a3417.speaker: Russia's foreign ministry
a3417.name: Russia's foreign ministry
a3417.speech: Said Quenelle's press credentials were not renewed in retaliation for France's refusal to issue press visas to journalists from Komsomolskaya Pravda.

a3417.speaker: Paris (French government)
a3417.name: Paris (French government)
a3417.speech: Accuses the Komsomolskaya Pravda journalists of being "agents of the Russian intelligence services."

a3417.speaker: Russian authorities (charges against Nadezhda Kevorkova)
a3417.name: Russian authorities (charges against Nadezhda Kevorkova)
a3417.speech: Arrested Middle East specialist Nadezhda Kevorkova in May 2024, accusing her of "justifying terrorism" in two posts on her Telegram account dating to 2018 and 2021.

a3417.speaker: Washington (US government)
a3417.name: Washington (US government)
a3417.speech: Denounced as trumped-up the espionage charges on which Moscow sentenced US journalist Evan Gershkovich to 16 years in jail.

a3549.speaker: Donors (international donors to the Horn of Africa drought response)
a3549.name: Donors (international donors to the Horn of Africa drought response)
a3549.speech: Have pledged 1.39 billion dollars for humanitarian and development response to the drought in the Horn of Africa that has left more than 15 million people severely food insecure across Ethiopia, Kenya and Somalia.

a3549.speaker: US government
a3549.name: US government
a3549.speech: Has pledged over 200 million dollars in assistance through the US Agency for International Development (USAID) and the Department of State to provide emergency food assistance to millions of people struggling to meet basic food, water, agriculture, and livestock needs amid the unprecedented drought in the region.

a3549.speaker: Canadian government
a3549.name: Canadian government
a3549.speech: Says it will provide over 73 million dollars.

a3641.speaker: US State Department
a3641.name: US State Department
a3641.speech: Described the gathering as a “targeted” follow-up to the 17th US-Africa Business Summit held last week in Luanda—which saw over $2.5 billion in agreements signed.

a3641.speaker: Documents cited by Reuters and The Washington Post
a3641.name: Documents cited by Reuters and The Washington Post
a3641.speech: According to the documents, Senegal, Mauritania, Gabon, and Liberia—whose leaders are currently in Washington—appeared on a list sent to African foreign ministries in mid-June; the justification for the potential migration restrictions cites “problems with the reliability” of identity documents and “administrative fraud.”

a3641.speaker: Dr. Alioune Aboutalib Lo, researcher at the AKEM Center in Istanbul
a3641.name: Dr. Alioune Aboutalib Lo
a3641.title: researcher at the AKEM Center in Istanbul
a3641.speech: Observes, “The presence of these five Atlantic-bound states reflects the importance the United States places on controlling coasts vital to maritime trade, rich in resources in a region marked by Russo-Chinese competition.” ; suggests that the establishment of Russian military bases, arms deliveries via Conakry, and military agreements with Togo and Sao Tome and Principe are causing significant concern in Washington and among its NATO allies.

a3641.speaker: Dr. Alioune Aboutalib Lo, researcher at the AKEM Center in Istanbul
a3641.name: Dr. Alioune Aboutalib Lo
a3641.title: researcher at the AKEM Center in Istanbul
a3641.speech: Says Senegal's posture of sovereignty—Prime Minister Ousmane Sonko's cancellation of a sports training program in the United States following a visa refusal, and the priority given to a visit to Beijing—“cannot leave Washington indifferent.”

a3641.speaker: Dr. Alioune Aboutalib Lo, researcher at the AKEM Center in Istanbul
a3641.name: Dr. Alioune Aboutalib Lo
a3641.title: researcher at the AKEM Center in Istanbul
a3641.speech: Facing what he describes as Trump's unpredictability and persistent asymmetry in relations, recommends “better African coordination to gain more leverage in the negotiations.”

a3713.speaker: Staff at the HIV/AIDS treatment centre in Kampala
a3713.name: Staff at the HIV/AIDS treatment centre in Kampala
a3713.speech: Say the usual daily influx of around 50 patients has all but dried up, with antiretroviral drugs piling up unused.

a3713.speaker: Andrew Tendo, resident medical officer at the US-funded clinic in Kampala
a3713.name: Andrew Tendo
a3713.title: resident medical officer at the US-funded clinic in Kampala
a3713.speech: Warned that new waves of HIV infections were forming even as vulnerable people stayed away from treatment centres, afraid of being identified and arrested under the new laws: “The LGBT community in Uganda is on lockdown now. They don't have preventive services. They cannot access condoms ... they cannot access ARTs (antiretrovirals)” ; said that now, when patients do come in, it's often out of absolute necessity, adding that the HIV cases presenting had become more severe as people skipped treatments.

a3713.speaker: Andrew Tendo, resident medical officer at the Kampala clinic run by Icebreakers Uganda
a3713.name: Andrew Tendo
a3713.title: resident medical officer at the Kampala clinic run by Icebreakers Uganda
a3713.speech: Said he understood the fears of LGBTQ people in Uganda who often endured painful lives, featuring rejection by their families and arrests: “The majority of these people, like transgender or queer people, have gone through a lot already. They wouldn't want to be in a place where they can be raided or detained at any time.”

a3713.speaker: Uganda AIDS Commission (state-run)
a3713.name: Uganda AIDS Commission (state-run)
a3713.speech: According to the commission, 1.4 million people in Uganda live with the virus and 17 000 die a year as a result of its ravages.

a3713.speaker: US official (unnamed)
a3713.name: US official (unnamed)
a3713.speech: Suggested that the law would reverse the country's gains fighting HIV/AIDS.

a3713.speaker: Uganda's Health Minister
a3713.name: Uganda's Health Minister
a3713.speech: Disputed a suggestion from a US official that the law would reverse the country's gains fighting HIV/AIDS, saying last week that the government would ensure that prevention programmes would remain accessible to those that needed them.

a3713.speaker: Ugandan health ministry
a3713.name: Ugandan health ministry
a3713.speech: Declined to comment for this article.

a3713.speaker: Mary Borgman, country director for the US President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR)
a3713.name: Mary Borgman
a3713.title: country director for the US President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR)
a3713.speech: Said the trend of HIV patients staying away from treatment centres is being mirrored on a national level, and that fear had increasingly been deterring people from coming in for treatment ever since the anti-gay bill was introduced in parliament in March ; said the American government was acutely aware of the impact any funding cuts would have on vulnerable communities, including LGBTQ Ugandans: “The review is around whether we can operate within the environment that we are provided with”, without elaborating on specific legal concerns.

a3713.speaker: 27-year-old gay man, patient at the Kampala clinic (anonymous, asked not to be identified for fear of being targeted by authorities)
a3713.name: 27-year-old gay man
a3713.title: patient at the Kampala clinic (anonymous, asked not to be identified for fear of being targeted by authorities)
a3713.speech: Said he despaired at the new legislation: “I felt so sad when the law was enacted because we fear PEPFAR will cut off funding for the free services we have been receiving.”

a3713.speaker: PEPFAR (programme estimates)
a3713.name: PEPFAR (programme estimates)
a3713.speech: Estimates its support for the scale-up of antiretroviral treatments in Uganda helped avert nearly 600 000 HIV-related deaths between 2004 and 2022.

a3713.speaker: Lillian Mworeko, East African regional coordinator for the International Community of Women living with HIV/AIDS
a3713.name: Lillian Mworeko
a3713.title: East African regional coordinator for the International Community of Women living with HIV/AIDS
a3713.speech: Said some providers feared that offering medical services to LGBTQ patients could be classed as “promoting” homosexuality, an offence punishable by 20 years in prison under the new law.

a3931.speaker: Dr Benedictus Freeman, USFS Liberia Country Coordinator
a3931.name: Dr Benedictus Freeman
a3931.title: USFS Liberia Country Coordinator
a3931.speech: “As part of the response to address illegal timber trafficking in Liberia, the US Forest Service is providing technical and logistical support to strengthen the capacity of in-country stakeholders, including government ministries, agencies and civil society organizations to achieve Liberia’s policy objectives.”

a3931.speaker: Moses Wenyanpulu, Forestry Development Authority (FDA) Research and Development Department
a3931.name: Moses Wenyanpulu
a3931.title: Forestry Development Authority (FDA) Research and Development Department
a3931.speech: “A lot was achieved in wood anatomy” ; “Like every human, every wood species has a unique and distinct fingerprint called anatomical features found within the wood structure. Understanding these features are very critical to properly identifying timber or lumber.”

a3978.speaker: Yekeh Kolubah, Representative for Montserrado County District #10
a3978.name: Yekeh Kolubah
a3978.title: Representative for Montserrado County District #10
a3978.speech: Receiving the microphone, instead of addressing Speaker Koon, said: “Mr. Deputy Speaker…” ; continued to rain invectives on Speaker Koon, stating that as far as he is concerned, Fonati Koffa remains the legitimate Speaker of the 55th Legislature, and that he won’t ever sit under a “junta” leadership ; “Let me tell you something today. The Supreme Court ruling is very clear. Richard Koon is not the Speaker of this House; and he can never be the Speaker of this House. I will come here again on Thursday. I will disrupt until they can respect the Supreme Court ruling. These people, they are juntas. As long as they keep behaving like juntas, I will keep dealing with them.”

a3978.speaker: Sekou Kalasco Damaro, special aide to former President George Weah
a3978.name: Sekou Kalasco Damaro
a3978.title: special aide to former President George Weah
a3978.speech: Said it is good that Representative Kolubah got a taste of his own medicine: “During the CDC Regime, Yekeh was given the stage to shine, his rights were respected and the government made sure that he was never harmed. I, personally, can attest to the day President Weah threatened his officials and warned them about going after Yekeh. He told one of his officials in a private chat room that if anything happens to Yekeh, he will face unimaginable consequences, yet Yekeh took Pres. Weah’s kindness for granted. Now he’s been treated the complete opposite by the government he brought to power. He has been beaten, tear gassed, pepper sprayed and dragged by state security on several occasions. Never take a powerful man’s kindness as weakness. Chicken coming home to roost doesn’t make me sad, it makes me glad.”

a3978.speaker: Shedrick Mondyu, member of the public
a3978.name: Shedrick Mondyu
a3978.title: member of the public
a3978.speech: “Yekeh Kolubah, please go ahead and tell the Supreme Court to reject their budget line in the national budget, since it was passed by a junta majority block of the House of Representatives.”

a3978.speaker: James Yuwolo Clarke, Sr., member of the public
a3978.name: James Yuwolo Clarke
a3978.title: Sr., member of the public
a3978.speech: “Are you the one to enforce the Supreme Court ruling? Did the court ask you to enforce its ruling, or you are the sheriff for the court, Mr. Noise Maker.”

a3978.speaker: Isaac Fatorma, Jr., member of the public
a3978.name: Isaac Fatorma
a3978.title: Jr., member of the public
a3978.speech: “Stranger has many laws, but the host has only one. Since you will keep disrupting, you will be pushed out everyday. Lastly, you will be flogged.”

a3978.speaker: Adama Mansaray, member of the public
a3978.name: Adama Mansaray
a3978.title: member of the public
a3978.speech: “Do you see Representative Abu Kamara, Representative Seboe Dixon and other lawmakers who were blacklisted coming here to cuss and disturb? The trouble Yekeh is looking for he will get it.”

a4092.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of the Republic of Mozambique
a4092.name: Daniel Chapo
a4092.title: President of the Republic of Mozambique
a4092.speech: Assured that Mozambique will begin receiving from the United States an injectable HIV vaccine every six months, and said he had sealed three important commitments during his visit: “The American government has approved ten countries in the world that can benefit from the latest medicine for the treatment of HIV. This medicine, which the American Government approved for ten countries in the world, of which Mozambique is one, is a great advance, because our brothers and sisters living with HIV have to take pills every day, but this medicine is a vaccine, that is, it is injectable and only has to be administered every six months,” adding that the vaccine has already been tested.

a4092.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of the Republic of Mozambique
a4092.name: Daniel Chapo
a4092.title: President of the Republic of Mozambique
a4092.speech: Thanked the United States for announcing the continuation of the Millennium Challenge Corporation project: “As you know very well, when the Trump administration took power, it took some decisions on cuts related, for example, to USAID support; there was also the cut to the MCC (...) also in the case of the MCC, the American Government continued making cuts in all the countries of Southern Africa. The only country for which they said the project can be implemented in the region is Mozambique. Therefore, Mozambique is the only survivor of the MCC.”

a4092.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of the Republic of Mozambique / Head of State
a4092.name: Daniel Chapo
a4092.title: President of the Republic of Mozambique / Head of State
a4092.speech: During Mozambique’s presence at the United Nations, argued for greater African representation, including a permanent seat on the United Nations Security Council.

a4102.speaker: USAID chief (unnamed in article text)
a4102.name: USAID chief (unnamed in article text)
a4102.speech: “There were 1.2 million AIDS-related deaths in 2014, but that number was down from 1.3 million the previous year and from a peak of two million in 2005. The actual number of new infections has also decreased to two million in 2014 compared with 2.1 million in 2013 and 3.1 million at their peak in 2000,” he said officially opening the two-day New Directions in Global Health held at the Mowana Safari Lodge.

a4228.speaker: Ronnie Shikapwasha, Zambian Minister of Information and Broadcasting Services / Chief Government spokesperson
a4228.name: Ronnie Shikapwasha
a4228.title: Zambian Minister of Information and Broadcasting Services / Chief Government spokesperson
a4228.speech: Refuted the allegation that he received money from Kasama Central member of Parliament Geoffrey Mwamba; said Mr Mwamba should not malign him because he has nothing to do with the case the PF parliamentarian is facing; said Mr Mwamba should know that when he was helping MMD members to campaign in 2006, he was doing so on the basis that he was a friend of the party; said it is not right for Mr Mwamba to start attacking people who have nothing to do with the allegations he is facing.

a4228.speaker: Ronnie Shikapwasha, Zambian Minister of Information and Broadcasting Services / Chief Government spokesperson
a4228.name: Ronnie Shikapwasha
a4228.title: Zambian Minister of Information and Broadcasting Services / Chief Government spokesperson
a4228.speech: Said in an interview on December 13 that while he has known Mr Mwamba for a long time, he has had no business dealings with him; said it is not possible for him to have received money from Mr Mwamba, having known the man’s background for a long time.

a4228.speaker: Ronnie Shikapwasha, Zambian Minister of Information and Broadcasting Services / Chief Government spokesperson
a4228.name: Ronnie Shikapwasha
a4228.title: Zambian Minister of Information and Broadcasting Services / Chief Government spokesperson
a4228.speech: Said it is morally wrong for Mr Mwamba to even have mentioned the name of late President Mwanawasa in his submissions to DEC; said Mr Mwamba and the Mwanawasa family have been close friends, and the late President had defended him in many cases ; “So, if he gave Mr Sata US$100,000, let him not drag other people into it. We cannot be part of the transaction that was conducted between him and his party leader”

a4228.speaker: Edward Mumbi, former Patriotic Front secretary general
a4228.name: Edward Mumbi
a4228.title: former Patriotic Front secretary general
a4228.speech: Advised Mr Mwamba, popularly known as GBM, to concentrate on defending himself against certain allegations made against him; said the attempt by Mr Mwamba to tell Zambians that he has been distributing his money to people will not help him: “The quoted statement that I am among the people who benefited from Mr Mwamba’s generosity is not true. The attempt by Mr Mwamba to tell Zambians that he gave Mr Sata money should be the issue he should concentrate on, and not lying against other people”

a4228.speaker: Edward Mumbi, former Patriotic Front secretary general
a4228.name: Edward Mumbi
a4228.title: former Patriotic Front secretary general
a4228.speech: Said Mr Mwamba has started contradicting Mr Sata’s statement by revealing that he had personally taken the US$100,000 cash to Mr Sata’s house when the latter has given a statement that the transaction was handled by the bank.

a4228.speaker: Geoffrey Mwamba, Kasama Central member of Parliament (submission to the Drug Enforcement Commission, as reported)
a4228.name: Geoffrey Mwamba
a4228.title: Kasama Central member of Parliament (submission to the Drug Enforcement Commission, as reported)
a4228.speech: In his submission to the Drug Enforcement Commission (DEC) on the US$100,000 given to Mr Sata, was reported to have alleged that Gen Shikapwasha was among the people who received money from him for campaigns, and was also reported to have told the DEC that former PF secretary general Mr Mumbi is among other people who received money from him.

a4274.speaker: 2022 Afrobarometer survey
a4274.name: 2022 Afrobarometer survey
a4274.speech: Highlighted public dissatisfaction with governance, with 57% of Malawians expressing discontent with democracy's performance due to economic mismanagement and corruption.

a4274.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a4274.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a4274.speech: Estimates $986 million in debt relief is needed by 2027.

a4274.speaker: World Bank's Malawi Economic Monitor
a4274.name: World Bank's Malawi Economic Monitor
a4274.speech: Highlighted the need to deepen fiscal decentralisation to improve service delivery and reach vulnerable households.

a4493.speaker: Observers (unnamed)
a4493.name: Observers (unnamed)
a4493.speech: Warn that a delay by Chakwera in conceding defeat to Mutharika could compromise peace and democratic stability in Malawi.

a4493.speaker: Electoral Commission of Malawi (MEC)
a4493.name: Electoral Commission of Malawi (MEC)
a4493.speech: Provisional figures published by the Electoral Commission indicate that Mutharika, representing the Democratic Progressive Party, has obtained around 66% of the valid votes counted so far, while Chakwera, the Malawi Congress Party candidate, is at only 24%, with results from a few districts still outstanding ; The Commission has committed to transparency and accuracy in its final count, amid heightened scrutiny following the annulment of Mutharika's 2019 victory on grounds of irregularities.

a4493.speaker: Malawi Council of Churches (MCC) and former president Bakili Muluzi
a4493.name: Malawi Council of Churches (MCC) and former president Bakili Muluzi
a4493.speech: Have publicly urged Chakwera to accept the results and congratulate Mutharika.

a4493.speaker: Billy Gamah, President of the Malawi Council of Churches (MCC)
a4493.name: Billy Gamah
a4493.title: President of the Malawi Council of Churches (MCC)
a4493.speech: Said that the remaining counts would probably not reverse the trend, describing a concession as a "statesmanlike gesture" likely to encourage calm and maturity among supporters: "We believe that an early acknowledgement, even before the official announcement, will show maturity, promote peace and help the country move forward without violence or unnecessary tensions," Gamah told local media.

a4493.speaker: Bakili Muluzi, former President of Malawi
a4493.name: Bakili Muluzi
a4493.title: former President of Malawi
a4493.speech: Echoed this sentiment in an interview with the private radio station Zodiak, saying that Chakwera should "let the country move forward" and reminding him that "there is life after the Presidential Palace".

a4509.speaker: Robert Lisinge, technology, innovation and connectivity expert
a4509.name: Robert Lisinge
a4509.title: technology, innovation and connectivity expert
a4509.speech: According to Lisinge, Africa's SMR ambitions can be achieved through "synchronised planning at regional and national levels": "There is a need to conceptualize and potentially develop regional nuclear projects that involve perhaps multiple countries."

a4509.speaker: Yohannes Hailu, Economic Affairs Officer at the UN Economic Commission for Africa
a4509.name: Yohannes Hailu
a4509.title: Economic Affairs Officer at the UN Economic Commission for Africa
a4509.speech: "Across the continent today, we have 15 percent of generation, 40 GW of power, that cannot be delivered simply because of infrastructure issues, curtailment, and grids not being available, sometimes for 800 to 1,000 hours per year."

a4509.speaker: Brian Dlamini, Planning Engineer for the Southern Africa Power Pool
a4509.name: Brian Dlamini
a4509.title: Planning Engineer for the Southern Africa Power Pool
a4509.speech: "SMRs could supply clean, reliable energy to creditworthy mining operations, enabling value addition to products for global markets."

a4509.speaker: Ghana's Nuclear Power Institute
a4509.name: Ghana's Nuclear Power Institute
a4509.speech: According to Ghana's Nuclear Power Institute, the country is also in the process of negotiating a "123 Agreement" with the U.S. for long-term civilian nuclear cooperation and trade.

a4509.speaker: BloombergNEF
a4509.name: BloombergNEF

a5101.speaker: G7 Foreign Ministers of Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the United Kingdom, the United States and the European Union (statement)
a5101.name: G7 Foreign Ministers of Canada
a5101.title: France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the United Kingdom, the United States and the European Union (statement)
a5101.speech: Have unequivocally condemned the continuing carnage in Sudan as the conflict clocks two years, and in a statement to APA on Wednesday denounced atrocities and grave human rights violations and abuses since the beginning of the devastating war between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF). ”As a direct result of the actions of the SAF and the RSF, the people of Sudan, especially women and children, are enduring the world’s largest humanitarian and displacement crises, and continued atrocities, including widespread conflict-related sexual violence, ethnically motivated attacks and reprisal killings. These must end immediately”

a5101.speaker: G7 Foreign Ministers (statement)
a5101.name: G7 Foreign Ministers (statement)
a5101.speech: Strongly condemned the RSF attacks in and around El Fasher on the Zamzam and Abu Shouk IDP camps, which have caused numerous casualties, including humanitarian workers, and called on civilians to be protected and allowed safe passage from war zones.

a5101.speaker: G7 members (statement)
a5101.name: G7 members (statement)
a5101.speech: Said they are disturbed by reports of the use of starvation of civilians as a method of warfare and reiterated that such actions are prohibited under international humanitarian law.

a5101.speaker: G7 Foreign Ministers (statement)
a5101.name: G7 Foreign Ministers (statement)
a5101.speech: ”We call on the warring parties to uphold their obligations under international humanitarian law and their commitments under the Jeddah Declaration, which include the crucial responsibility to distinguish at all times between civilians and combatants and between civilian objects and military targets” ; They urged all parties to the conflict to lift impediments to effective crossline humanitarian assistance, provide assurances of safety and security for local and international humanitarian actors, and allow humanitarian access through all border crossings into Sudan, including through South Sudan and Chad.

a5101.speaker: G7 Foreign Ministers (statement)
a5101.name: G7 Foreign Ministers (statement)
a5101.speech: Calling for an immediate and unconditional ceasefire, the G7 urged both the SAF and the RSF to engage meaningfully in serious, constructive negotiations where all external actors must cease any support that further fuels the conflict, in accordance with the Declaration of Principles adopted at the International Humanitarian Conference for Sudan and Neighbouring Countries in Paris in 2024 and the United Nations arms embargo on Darfur.

a5101.speaker: G7 Foreign Ministers (statement)
a5101.name: G7 Foreign Ministers (statement)
a5101.speech: ”For sustainable peace in Sudan, any resolution to the conflict must be rooted in the voices of Sudanese civilians. Women, youth, and civil society must be meaningfully included in all peace processes”

a5101.speaker: G7 members (statement)
a5101.name: G7 members (statement)
a5101.speech: While expressing support for the sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity of Sudan, said they will remain committed to deepening collective diplomatic efforts to bring about an end to the world’s largest humanitarian crisis and secure an end to the conflict, including through the London Sudan Conference.

a5126.speaker: Mark Toner, U.S. Ambassador to Liberia

By improving the LRA's capacity to collect taxes more efficiently, we are not only boosting revenue, we are supporting improvements in Liberia's public services–whether in healthcare, education or infrastructure. However, we need to ensure revenue transparency and accountability so that resources can be effectively utilized for the country's development. It is crucial for citizens to see the tangible benefits of their taxes.” ; Emphasized the importance of enhancing tax collection systems to boost revenue for Liberia's national development and highlighted the donation's role in improving operational efficiency and fostering public trust in the LRA.

The U.S. Government is proud to support Liberia in this important transition to VAT. Through the LEAD Activity, we will continue to work closely with LRA, particularly the Domestic Tax Department, to ensure the successful implementation of VAT. This support will include training and capacity building for staff and field offices, helping to create a more efficient and transparent tax system.”

Some economists and other experts have predicted that this can be done in two to three years. However, we are working overtime to ensure that we achieve that in a shorter time frame.” ; “LRA is currently working with the US government and other partners as we strive to improve our domestic revenue base in a way that will surmount our recurrent that has bedeviled our current plight because it is only through these means that we can carry out meaningful development that are enabled by locally collected revenues — which is the path to achieving the SDGs.”

a5126.speaker: James Dorbor Jallah, Commissioner General of the Liberia Revenue Authority (LRA)
a5126.name: James Dorbor Jallah
a5126.title: Commissioner General of the Liberia Revenue Authority (LRA)
a5126.speech: Acknowledged the substantial contribution of the US government to Liberia's domestic revenue generation: “The support from the US government has, over the years, contributed excessively to our domestic revenue generation. Right after the Liberian civil crisis, the nation's budget stood at a paltry US$80 million, but today, it is almost US$700 million. Back in the day, about 90 percent of the budget depended upon external support, but today, only US$40 million of the nearly US$700 million budget is sourced from outside.” ; “Most of our successes in this regard has been as a result of the enormous support we continue to receive from the US government and other partners.” ; “This support from USAID will significantly bolster our efforts to modernize our systems and improve tax collection, which is crucial for Liberia's development agenda.”

a5238.speaker: DG ECHO, UN OCHA and IOM (ECHO Daily Flash of 1 October 2025)

a5238.title: UN OCHA and IOM (ECHO Daily Flash of 1 October 2025)
a5238.speech: reported that between 26 August and 24 September, Cabo Delgado province has experienced a sharp rise in non-state armed group violent episodes, heavily affecting civilians in Ancuabe, Balama, Macomia, and Mocimboa da Praia; that 519 attacks have been recorded since January 2025, the highest number since the conflict began, with incidents including abductions, looting and killings; that over 20,000 people were displaced, including some 10,000 children, adding to the 57,000 people already displaced by attacks between late July and early August; that child protection risks are escalating, with many unaccompanied children lacking birth registration, restricting access to services and increasing exposure to harm, and reports also citing child killings and maiming due to improvised explosive devices as well as growing child marriage risks in displacement settings; that growing insecurity has also disrupted humanitarian operations, causing temporary aid suspensions in several areas; and that partners are assisting displaced populations in Mueda, Muidumbe, Ancuabe, Balama, and Montepuez through the NGO-led rapid response mechanism supported by DG ECHO, but others remain without support due to limited resources.

a5335.speaker: Liberian Education Reform Act of 2011 (legislation)
a5335.name: Liberian Education Reform Act of 2011 (legislation)
a5335.speech: Establishes that the Ministry of Education (MOE) has the power to certify, license, and accredit teachers, school administrators, and support staff, though it does not provide details on how often schools need to renew their licenses ; gives the Ministry the authority to monitor and ensure quality education in all schools (both public and private) and mandates the MOE to conduct inspections to evaluate schools based on established national standards, monitor teacher performance and ensure they are qualified and meet teaching standards, and evaluate students' performance in relation to curriculum objectives, using various assessment methods, including national exams such as the West African Senior School Certificate Examination (WASSCE).

a5408.speaker: Duma Boko, President of Botswana and Chairman of the African Leaders Malaria Alliance (ALMA)
a5408.name: Duma Boko
a5408.title: President of Botswana and Chairman of the African Leaders Malaria Alliance (ALMA)
a5408.speech: Speaking at the 38th African Union Summit in Addis Ababa, appealed to African nations to rise to the challenge presented by the suspension of USAID by mobilising their national resources to combat diseases like malaria, championing a new approach in which Africa should invest in its own health systems; acknowledged that the sudden suspension of global aid by the US government makes the fight against malaria "a tall order", but stressed that the continent should move on and adopt a response centred on continental cooperation: "The task before us is both challenging and urgent. Our progress has stalled, and the hard truth is that we are not on track." ; "A perfect storm of threats, insufficient resources, climate change, biological risks and humanitarian crises threaten to undermine our efforts. The upcoming global fund replenishment will determine whether we sustain our progress or fall further behind. The recent decision of the US government to suspend aid has without doubt knocked us further off track because we did not have sufficient time to prepare ourselves with lifesaving commodities (that are) either lying undistributed or with delayed delivery." ; "Securing the resources needed to combat malaria and fill those critical gaps with renewed energy is imperative. Africa must urgently rise to the challenge by mobilising domestic resources, including drawing down on resources in our emergency funds or increasing our health budget allocations." ; encouraged African countries to scale up financing through platforms such as the World Bank International Development Association (IDA) and the Green Climate Fund to ensure that national programmes are equipped to drive the malaria agenda forward.

a5551.speaker: Some other Ethiopian researchers
a5551.name: Some other Ethiopian researchers
a5551.speech: Argue that GMO crops are safe and a potential solution for the challenges facing global food production, climate change, population growth and competition for land.

a5551.speaker: Ethiopian Institute of Agricultural Research (EIAR)
a5551.name: Ethiopian Institute of Agricultural Research (EIAR)
a5551.speech: Said the report is a mistake and that the country did not approve the use of GMO seeds on a commercial level ; according to the institute, the experiment on maize and Enset (false banana), running since 2018, is going well as expected.

a5551.speaker: Tesfaye Disasa (PhD), Director of Agricultural Biotechnology at the Ethiopian Institute of Agricultural Research (EIAR)
a5551.name: Tesfaye Disasa (PhD)
a5551.title: Director of Agricultural Biotechnology at the Ethiopian Institute of Agricultural Research (EIAR)
a5551.speech: "GMO commercialization was started after the amendment of biosafety proclamation in 2015 (Proclamation No.896/2015). The only GMO at commercial stage is Bt-cotton which was approved for commercialization in 2018. The rest are under preliminary contained laboratory and Confined Field Trial (CFT). The mandate to approve or reject any application of GM crops goes to Forest, Environment and Climate Change Commission (EFCCC) the then Ministry of Forest, Environment and Climate Change."

a5551.speaker: Tesfaye Disasa (PhD), Director of Agricultural Biotechnology at EIAR
a5551.name: Tesfaye Disasa (PhD)
a5551.title: Director of Agricultural Biotechnology at EIAR
a5551.speech: On side effects: "In fact any new technologies have potential risks and require extensive studies before approving to use as food or feed. The most expensive component for commercialization of GM seeds is the cost associated with risk assessments... None of the frequently listed side effects from the use of GM products are supported by scientific evidence. We have been consuming GM products since its discovery but there is no tangible report on its side effect on human, animal and environment. In my view, any side effect of GMO should be supported with facts. We need to focus on institutional capacity building to generate more and more scientific facts."

a5551.speaker: Tesfaye Disasa (PhD), Director of Agricultural Biotechnology at EIAR
a5551.name: Tesfaye Disasa (PhD)
a5551.title: Director of Agricultural Biotechnology at EIAR
a5551.speech: On the claim that GMO is a new form of colonialism: "In my view, such kind of argument is outdated debate. It created unnecessary argument between those who support the technology and who don't care for the technology. It is better to develop an argument to make a cause for science and technology... Application of modern tools cannot negatively affect our natural resources and biodiversity rather it will enable us to develop efficient strategy to protect human health and natural resources." ; "So far a total of 70 countries have adopted biotech crops and cultivating over 191.7 million hectors of land globally. Ethiopia is currently at infant stage to be considered as one of GM producing countries. Only preliminary research activities are currently underway in a confined environment to test the efficacy of the genes... Let us advocate for science and technology not for chemical producing companies."

a5551.speaker: Tesfaye Disasa (PhD), Director of Agricultural Biotechnology at EIAR
a5551.name: Tesfaye Disasa (PhD)
a5551.title: Director of Agricultural Biotechnology at EIAR
a5551.speech: On European bans: "This is not true, majority of them are doing research on GMO and some of them are producing GM crops. Still majority of them are importing clearly labeled GM products from outside. There has been misplaced debate between North America and Europe on commercialization of GM crops... We are not the first African country to adopt GM crops. There are a number of African countries with huge natural resources which have started producing GM crops. So far no single death is reported as a result of GM consumption while millions of children are dying as a result of hunger and poverty."

a5551.speaker: Tesfaye Disasa (PhD), Director of Agricultural Biotechnology at EIAR
a5551.name: Tesfaye Disasa (PhD)
a5551.title: Director of Agricultural Biotechnology at EIAR
a5551.speech: On Burkina Faso's Bt-cotton experience: "Burkina Faso was one of the major Bt-cotton producers in Africa by 2014. Bt-cotton constituted 70% of all cultivated cotton by that time. Due to concern from textile industries about the length of fiber from the new Bt-cotton variety which was shorter than regular and they were having difficulty getting premium prices on the international market. I think it is better to identify whether the problem is due to technology failure or the type of varieties. Therefore, I am not in a position to conclude as the suspension of Bt-cotton by Burkina Faso government is as a result of technology failure... I don't think the same thing will be replicated here and there and I don't believe Ethiopia will face the same challenge."
