a5716.speech: In an earlier statement, he said there is no minimum price for the country's tobacco as each grade has its own minimum: "In Malawi, there are 52 grades for burley tobacco; 99 for flue-cured and virginia and 48 grades for dark-fired tobacco. A minimum price is set for each of these grades. This means there are 199 minimum prices of Malawi tobacco."

a5716.speaker: Christone Nyondo, Mwapata Institute research fellow
a5716.name: Christone Nyondo
a5716.title: Mwapata Institute research fellow
a5716.speech: Said in an interview on Tuesday that if prices offered at the tobacco floors persist, they could harm the country's foreign exchange reserves and trade balance; said this means that the Reserve Bank of Malawi may find it challenging to stabilise the kwacha, leading to increased import prices for essentials such as fuel, fertiliser and medicines.

a5716.speaker: Christone Nyondo, Mwapata Institute research fellow
a5716.name: Christone Nyondo
a5716.title: Mwapata Institute research fellow
a5716.speech: "The market structure is dominated by an oligopoly. Buyers can collude to maintain low prices while farmers, especially smallholders, have little bargaining power."

a5716.speaker: Tamani Nkhono-Mvula, agriculture policy development expert
a5716.name: Tamani Nkhono-Mvula
a5716.title: agriculture policy development expert
a5716.speech: Warned that if such pricing patterns persist, the country's fragile macroeconomic position could worsen. ; "The government should strengthen farmer cooperatives and create transparent price-setting mechanisms. Otherwise, farmers remain at the mercy of market forces beyond their control."

a5742.speaker: Teachers at Kawale Primary School, Chitipa District
a5742.name: Teachers at Kawale Primary School
a5742.title: Chitipa District
a5742.speech: Have thanked Karonga Diocese of the Catholic Church for constructing four teachers' houses.

a5742.speaker: Vincent Munyimbiri, head teacher of Kawale Primary School
a5742.name: Vincent Munyimbiri
a5742.title: head teacher of Kawale Primary School
a5742.speech: Said only five out of 36 teachers had houses at the school: "With the additional four houses, it means we now have nine teachers residing at the school. This will enhance efficient delivery of lessons. We appeal to other stakeholders to help construct more houses."

a5742.speaker: Ethel Kayuni, a beneficiary teacher
a5742.name: Ethel Kayuni
a5742.title: a beneficiary teacher
a5742.speech: Said she used to spend K3 000 daily on transport to school: "Preparation of lesson plans was difficult due to long distances and fatigue. Now, that is history. I am able to plan well and deliver lessons efficiently" ; also said the houses will motivate teachers to work hard.

a5742.speaker: Lino Nyirenda, diocesan education desk officer
a5742.name: Lino Nyirenda
a5742.title: diocesan education desk officer
a5742.speech: Said the diocese received funding from United States of America-based Cross Catholic Outreach and constructed two duplex staff houses at K163.4 million and two classroom blocks with desks, toilets and textbooks at K122.2 million: "The construction of these classroom blocks mean that children who were learning under trees have extra space and desks to sit at, thereby increasing performance while the four houses can now accommodate four more teachers who will have more time to prepare for lessons."

a5771.speaker: Dumisani Msibi, Group Managing Director, Eswatini Development Finance Corporation (FINCORP)
a5771.name: Dumisani Msibi
a5771.title: Group Managing Director, Eswatini Development Finance Corporation (FINCORP)
a5771.speech: Announced that FINCORP has sustained more than 15 000 jobs in the past 15 years through its financing initiatives; said the corporation remained committed to empowering entrepreneurs and building communities through access to finance and training; revealed that FINCORP had injected E300 000 into this year’s business shower, bringing the total investment into JA programmes to about E1 million: “These resources are not just numbers. They are transforming lives, uplifting families, and empowering communities across the Kingdom.”

a5771.speaker: Dumisani Msibi, Group Managing Director, Eswatini Development Finance Corporation (FINCORP)
a5771.name: Dumisani Msibi
a5771.title: Group Managing Director, Eswatini Development Finance Corporation (FINCORP)
a5771.speech: Disclosed that about E1.5 billion is currently circulating in the hands of Emaswati entrepreneurs supported by FINCORP’s products and services: “This is capital that is developing individuals economically and ensuring that their families and communities’ benefit.”

a5771.speaker: 2023 Blended FinScope MSME Survey
a5771.name: 2023 Blended FinScope MSME Survey
a5771.speech: Showed that Eswatini is home to approximately 70 000 enterprises employing over 90 000 people and contributing nearly 50 percent of the country’s gross domestic product (GDP).

a5771.speaker: MSME Policy 2024–2029
a5771.name: MSME Policy 2024–2029
a5771.speech: Acknowledged FINCORP’s contribution in addressing financing barriers, especially for micro and rural enterprises.

a5771.speaker: Dumisani Msibi, Group Managing Director, FINCORP
a5771.name: Dumisani Msibi
a5771.title: Group Managing Director, FINCORP
a5771.speech: Stated that “Young people are the heartbeat of our nation, yet too often, they face one of the greatest barriers to entrepreneurship and access to finance due to lack of collateral,” and explained that FINCORP had signed an agreement with the Centre for Financial Inclusion (CFI) to provide additional support for young entrepreneurs, covering 20 per cent per borrower and supporting loans of up to E250 000 for youth between the ages of 18 and 35: “Finance alone is not enough, and we believe that this initiative is more than just a program, but a Launchpad for young entrepreneurs.”

a5771.speaker: Dumisani Msibi, Group Managing Director, FINCORP
a5771.name: Dumisani Msibi
a5771.title: Group Managing Director, FINCORP
a5771.speech: Said the Citizen Economic Empowerment Act and the Business One Stop Shop (BOSS) had set the stage for MSMEs, especially youth-led businesses, to enter the market with fewer barriers, greater support and more confidence: “The future of Eswatini’s economy cannot be reinvigorated by a few large companies here and there, but by thousands of existing and future entrepreneurs including those gathered here today,” ; “When you succeed, communities prosper; when you thrive, the nation thrives.”

a5771.speaker: Manqoba Khumalo, Minister of Commerce, Industry and Trade
a5771.name: Manqoba Khumalo
a5771.title: Minister of Commerce, Industry and Trade
a5771.speech: Described the JA Business Shower as instrumental in enhancing MSME growth and encouraging investment; commended Junior Achievement Eswatini for creating opportunities for young people to participate in meaningful economic activity during the Eswatini International Trade Fair; said youth empowerment remained a government priority: “The EITF serves as an excellent platform for traders to introduce or promote themselves, complemented by various value-adding activities such as business seminars that run throughout the duration of the show.”

a5771.speaker: Manqoba Khumalo, Minister of Commerce, Industry and Trade
a5771.name: Manqoba Khumalo
a5771.title: Minister of Commerce, Industry and Trade
a5771.speech: Assured young entrepreneurs that government support would continue: “Government shall continue to support JA Eswatini through an annual subvention of E500 000 for promoting youth MSMEs and cooperatives in schools and out of school,” and explained that the Ministry of Economic Planning and Development had worked closely with his ministry to ensure financial support for programmes such as JA financial literacy and entrepreneurship, as well as cooperatives development; he further encouraged young people to make use of existing support mechanisms.

a5771.speaker: Phetsile Masilela, Executive Director, JA Eswatini
a5771.name: Phetsile Masilela
a5771.title: Executive Director, JA Eswatini
a5771.speech: Said the annual government subvention had enabled the organisation to implement financial literacy and entrepreneurship training for both in-school and out-of-school youth; noted that the support came at a time when JA Eswatini was affected by the termination of USAID grants to the country.

a5771.speaker: Phetsile Masilela, Executive Director, JA Eswatini
a5771.name: Phetsile Masilela
a5771.title: Executive Director, JA Eswatini
a5771.speech: Said JA would host a Business Masterclass facilitated by different stakeholders; revealed that 35 applications had been received from young entrepreneurs seeking to pitch their businesses for seed capital support through the business shower, of which 10 business plans were shortlisted with five set to receive funding; emphasised that the business shower had grown into a platform where youth could not only access financial support but also gain mentorship and skills.

a5943.speaker: Dieudonne Disi, Rwandan long distance runner
a5943.name: Dieudonne Disi
a5943.title: Rwandan long distance runner
a5943.speech: “When I was barely 13, I lost my family (both parents and six siblings) in the 1994 Genocide against Tutsi. They were killed right in my face.” ; “I also do it to shape a good life for myself that I was almost denied in 1994,” he told Saturday Sport by email on Thursday from his base in France.

a5943.speaker: Dieudonne Disi, Rwandan long distance runner
a5943.name: Dieudonne Disi
a5943.title: Rwandan long distance runner
a5943.speech: Narrates how he switched sports: “In football, I was not getting a first slot in my former schools' teams no matter how much I tried to impress the coaches. I had a classmate called Pacifique Ayubusa, who was an athletics star at school and a national team runner in 1997. With his help and advice, I switched from football to athletics.”

a5943.speaker: Dieudonne Disi, Rwandan long distance runner
a5943.name: Dieudonne Disi
a5943.title: Rwandan long distance runner
a5943.speech: Disclosed: “Ever since making my international debut in 1999, I have gone on to compete in over 200 competitions and I have been on podium for over 150 times. I have also been able to travel to 82 countries worldwide.”

a5943.speaker: Dieudonne Disi, Rwandan long distance runner
a5943.name: Dieudonne Disi
a5943.title: Rwandan long distance runner
a5943.speech: Said he is planning to retire soon: “I'm serving my last days in competitive athletics, because I believe it's time to move on to a different challenge. If all goes well, I want to participate in one competition before announcing my official retirement but I don't know exactly when.”

a5943.speaker: Dieudonne Disi, Rwandan long distance runner
a5943.name: Dieudonne Disi
a5943.title: Rwandan long distance runner
a5943.speech: Says watching his family being killed on April 23, 1994, will forever be the saddest memory that he can never forget: “Every time the issue comes up, I feel pain in my chest.”

a6039.speaker: Development experts on Liberia
a6039.name: Development experts on Liberia
a6039.speech: Have long argued that the country's transformation and growth lie in agriculture, not only in terms of food security and self-reliance but also in job creation and economic independence — the general fight against poverty ; according to the experts, Liberia is stuck in the abyss of poverty and socioeconomic stagnation because the sector is accorded mere rhetoric and slogans, grossly downplayed and untapped.

a6039.speaker: Dr. J. Alexander Nuetah, Minister of Agriculture of Liberia
a6039.name: Dr. J. Alexander Nuetah
a6039.title: Minister of Agriculture of Liberia
a6039.speech: "The message was clear," he always says. "Liberia's agricultural transformation begins with every seed planted, every innovation embraced, and every partnership forged."

a6039.speaker: Dr. J. Alexander Nuetah, Minister of Agriculture of Liberia
a6039.name: Dr. J. Alexander Nuetah
a6039.title: Minister of Agriculture of Liberia
a6039.speech: Said his incumbency strives, with the National Agriculture Development Plan as his roadmap at the cost of US$717 million, to remove "constraints that affect our farmers and other value-chain actors including low productivity, poor rural infrastructure that limits access to market, limited access to improved production techniques and postharvest-handling technologies do not only lead to negative climate-change effects but also high postharvest losses, and lack access to affordable credit for value-chain development."

a6039.speaker: A staff member of the Ministry of Agriculture (anonymous)
a6039.name: A staff member of the Ministry of Agriculture (anonymous)
a6039.speech: Quotes the Minister saying that food security and the overall agriculture crusade would amount to nothing until bureaucrats and technicians leave their desks, move upcountry to the rural people, acquaint and supply them with modern technology and skills and financially capitalize and create market for them ; "Our minister is sleeplessly committed in achieving that, which is why he shows leadership by example, always creating programs for and reaching out to those who matter – the farmers."

a6039.speaker: National and foreign partners including FAO, USAID, IFAD, the World Bank, and ECOWAS
a6039.name: National and foreign partners including FAO
a6039.title: USAID, IFAD, the World Bank, and ECOWAS
a6039.speech: Have reaffirmed their commitment to supporting his flagship program, Liberia's National Agriculture Development Plan (NADP 2024–2030).

a6043.speaker: Tucker Carlson, journalist, and JD Vance, Republican vice-presidential running mate
a6043.name: Tucker Carlson
a6043.title: journalist, and JD Vance, Republican vice-presidential running mate
a6043.speech: Both advocate a minimalist foreign policy and are highly critical of American military interventions abroad.

a6043.speaker: Donald Trump, US presidential candidate
a6043.name: Donald Trump
a6043.title: US presidential candidate
a6043.speech: Calls the federal bureaucracy he intends to fight “the deep state,” and has said his administration would reduce the influence of the federal state.

a6122.speaker: Alassane Ouattara, President of Côte d'Ivoire
a6122.name: Alassane Ouattara
a6122.title: President of Côte d'Ivoire
a6122.speech: Said at a press briefing that they had “discussed at length the security situation” in the sub-region, which “remains very worrying, as well as the socio-political situation in the Sahel”; “We noted the need to provide assistance to these brother countries to enable them to meet humanitarian and security needs. We trust you, Mr President, that in your discussions with these brother countries you will be able to convince them to remain in ECOWAS, because the future of the peoples of West Africa is at stake.” ; “I would also like to make an appeal to the AES countries to say that we are better as 15 than as three, so I hope that President Mahama's appeal can be heard by these three brother countries, two of which are neighbours of Côte d'Ivoire, so that we can continue together within ECOWAS.”

a6122.speaker: Alassane Ouattara, President of Côte d'Ivoire
a6122.name: Alassane Ouattara
a6122.title: President of Côte d'Ivoire
a6122.speech: Welcomed the “excellent discussion” in which they addressed “matters of common interest, in particular in the areas of defence, security and the cocoa economy”, as well as “questions relating to mines and energy, and the major ECOWAS projects such as the Abidjan-Lagos corridor and the common currency, the Eco”; added: “Regarding bilateral cooperation, we reaffirmed our common will to support the Côte d'Ivoire-Ghana Cocoa Initiative and to strengthen cooperation between Ghana and Côte d'Ivoire in mining and energy and in the fight against illegal gold panning”; “We have committed to supporting and working towards the implementation of the Côte d'Ivoire-Ghana strategic partnership agreement, a privileged instrument of cooperation, signed in 2017 in Accra.”

a6122.speaker: Alassane Ouattara, President of Côte d'Ivoire
a6122.name: Alassane Ouattara
a6122.title: President of Côte d'Ivoire
a6122.speech: On the reduction of American funding, admitted “it is true that it is a very large part of international financing (64%)”, recalling that Côte d'Ivoire benefits from MCC financing as well as funding for the fight against malaria and AIDS; “we have taken measures, at our level, to continue financing all these projects while waiting for the United States to resume things after the audit that is under way. We are (nevertheless) confident”; “The United States has always been a friendly country to Côte d'Ivoire and I consider that the outcome of the review by the American government (will be favourable) and that disbursements will resume for Côte d'Ivoire.”

a6122.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6122.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6122.title: President of Ghana
a6122.speech: Maintained that “there is still the possibility of bringing our brother countries back home. It is better to stay in a group of 15 than to stay in a group of three”; insisted that “these are countries that matter in the sub-region” and that it is important for them to “remain in the ECOWAS space, insofar as their populations are on the border lines for economic interests. And as I say, it is always better to be in a group of 15 than in a group of three.”

a6122.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6122.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6122.title: President of Ghana
a6122.speech: On US aid: “the United States has the right to review its cooperation strategy, to see how it might direct its funding. I think this is also an opportunity for us to see how we can rely on ourselves”; said he had heard there would be “a reduction (in funding) from USAID”, considering that “this is for us an opportunity to also review our economic strategies.”

a6256.speaker: Presidency of the Republic of Mozambique (statement)
a6256.name: Presidency of the Republic of Mozambique (statement)
a6256.speech: Indicates that the head of state will also hold a popular rally, meet with the private sector representatives including investors in the oil, gas and mining sectors, and liaise with non-governmental organizations.

a6379.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6379.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6379.title: President of Ghana
a6379.speech: "We condemn the loss of human life and the forced displacements, with the dramatic consequences that result from them. I call for peace, for unhindered humanitarian access, for the protection of civilians and for respect for international humanitarian law," the Ghanaian head of state declared in his address.

a6379.speaker: Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Ghana
a6379.name: Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa
a6379.title: Minister of Foreign Affairs of Ghana
a6379.speech: Delivered the opening speech at the official handover ceremony at Jubilee House in Accra.

a6379.speaker: Abdalafatah A. K. Alsattari, Ambassador of Palestine to Ghana
a6379.name: Abdalafatah A. K. Alsattari
a6379.title: Ambassador of Palestine to Ghana
a6379.speech: Receiving the donation, welcomed a gesture of solidarity by the Ghanaian people in these difficult times.

a6379.speaker: Hamas
a6379.name: Hamas
a6379.speech: According to Hamas, more than 60,000 Palestinians have been killed.

a6379.speaker: Humanitarian agencies
a6379.name: Humanitarian agencies
a6379.speech: Denounce severe restrictions on the delivery of aid, exacerbated by insecurity and administrative blockages; several humanitarian convoys have been prevented from entering or have been targeted, making the situation even more critical for civilian populations.

a6584.speaker: Milward Tobias, economist
a6584.name: Milward Tobias
a6584.title: economist
a6584.speech: Says one would be correct to say Malawi has delegated development to foreigners given the fact that nearly all major and impactful development projects are financed by development partners: "There is potential to free up and channel more domestic resources toward development projects. There is a lot of luxury and wastage that when sanitised, fiscal space will be created. That, however, requires strong and competent political leadership."

a6584.speaker: Bertha Bangara Chikadza, President of the Economics Association of Malawi (Ecama)
a6584.name: Bertha Bangara Chikadza
a6584.title: President of the Economics Association of Malawi (Ecama)
a6584.speech: Believes this would be an oversimplification of the current situation; according to Chikadza, the development budget allocations from 2022-23 to 2025-26 show an average of 77 percent of actual spending being financed by donors: "This indicates primary dependence on foreign funding for infrastructure, key social programmes and other economic initiatives." ; "It poses a risk to development projects as some donor countries have pulled out some of their support and others signal to move in a similar direction." She was quick to note that while this may indicate a certain level of dependence, the government still sets the budget priorities to ensure they are in line with Malawi's long-term development targets, and implementation often involves local agents.

a6584.speaker: Velli Nyirongo, Scotland-based economist
a6584.name: Velli Nyirongo
a6584.title: Scotland-based economist
a6584.speech: Said that, technically, Malawi has effectively delegated much of its development responsibilities to foreign entities due to its heavy reliance on external financing for development projects; said in recent years foreign aid has constituted up to 73 percent of the country's development budget, reflecting a dependency that undermines domestic ownership and long-term sustainability: "Aligning budgetary frameworks with long-term national strategies such as MW2063 can further ensure resources are directed toward productive sectors. By prioritising sustainable domestic financing, Malawi can build a self-reliant and resilient economy."

a6584.speaker: Marvin Banda, economist
a6584.name: Marvin Banda
a6584.title: economist
a6584.speech: Said it is not that Malawi has delegated development to foreigners but, rather, that these are the types of projects development partners want to finance in terms of development.

a6584.speaker: Williams Banda, Treasury spokesperson
a6584.name: Williams Banda
a6584.title: Treasury spokesperson
a6584.speech: Asked for more time before he could comment on the matter.

a6584.speaker: Lazarus Chakwera, President of Malawi (foreword to the Malawi 2063 document)
a6584.name: Lazarus Chakwera
a6584.title: President of Malawi (foreword to the Malawi 2063 document)
a6584.speech: Says donors continue to support Malawi's development programmes.

a6584.speaker: Thom Khanje, National Planning Commission spokesperson
a6584.name: Thom Khanje
a6584.title: National Planning Commission spokesperson
a6584.speech: Said the Malawi 2063 envisions a Malawi that is inclusively wealthy and self-reliant by 2063; said, however, that the vision also recognises that this cannot be achieved overnight and that as a country Malawi has to work progressively to achieve that: "As a country, therefore, we'll continue to rely on development partners to support us in our development endeavours while we are working tirelessly to become inclusively wealthy and self-reliant."

a6584.speaker: Mike Mlombwa, President of the Indigenous Businesses Association of Malawi
a6584.name: Mike Mlombwa
a6584.title: President of the Indigenous Businesses Association of Malawi
a6584.speech: Said Malawi has struggled to effectively finance its development architecture because most Malawians remain in poverty.

a6669.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a6669.name: Donald Trump
a6669.title: US President
a6669.speech: During the 2024 election vowed to begin his second term by controlling legal migration and deporting those in the US without legal status, and has vowed to reinstate his travel ban.

a6669.speaker: Experts (unnamed)
a6669.name: Experts (unnamed)
a6669.speech: Some experts have said Nigeria is likely to be one of the countries to be affected by the reinstated travel ban.

a6669.speaker: Femi Mimiko, professor of foreign policy at Obafemi Awolowo University
a6669.name: Femi Mimiko
a6669.title: professor of foreign policy at Obafemi Awolowo University
a6669.speech: Told PREMIUM TIMES that Nigeria can expect President Donald Trump's second administration to be generally unfavourable politically and economically, saying the president has scant respect for the continent, referring to it "as made up of shithole countries that he would rather keep out of the US": "Things are going to be a bit rough for Nigerian and African 'illegal immigrants,' because, shorn of all facade, much of the vituperations from Mr Trump on illegal immigration are directed at people of colour."

a6669.speaker: Health officials
a6669.name: Health officials
a6669.speech: Have described Robert Kennedy Jr's views as dangerous to public health.

a6669.speaker: Robert Kennedy Jr., nominee to lead the US Department of Health and Human Services
a6669.name: Robert Kennedy Jr.
a6669.title: nominee to lead the US Department of Health and Human Services
a6669.speech: Has consistently questioned the safety and efficacy of routine vaccines, including those for hepatitis B and influenza, and has propagated a debunked claim linking the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine to autism; also referred to the Covid vaccine as "the deadliest vaccine ever made," despite data showing it is overwhelmingly safe.

a6669.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a6669.name: Donald Trump
a6669.title: US President
a6669.speech: Has promised to sign an executive order declaring a national energy emergency, aiming to boost US oil and gas production and lower costs for US consumers.

a6669.speaker: Experts (unnamed)
a6669.name: Experts (unnamed)
a6669.speech: According to experts, if the U.S. ramps up its oil output it could potentially lower global oil prices and weaken OPEC's ability to control pricing through production cuts or quotas, as the market would become more competitive with US oil flooding the market.

a6669.speaker: Yinka Tella, spokesperson for the Nigerians in Diaspora Organisation (NiDO)
a6669.name: Yinka Tella
a6669.title: spokesperson for the Nigerians in Diaspora Organisation (NiDO)
a6669.speech: Said US oil production is unlikely to affect global trade, as the US is not concerned about oil exports but is more focused on producing enough oil for domestic use: "The US is not really into exports. The country is more concerned with producing enough for domestic consumption and storing it for rainy days. So, essentially, it cannot affect OPEC. Also, Nigeria's oil industry has changed with the establishment of the Dangote refinery and other private refineries that are in the way. Over time, we might not have much to export anymore."

a6669.speaker: Experts (unnamed)
a6669.name: Experts (unnamed)
a6669.speech: According to experts, the AGOA trade pact, which allows duty-free, quota-free access for African exports to the US, may face significant hurdles under the new administration.

a6669.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a6669.name: Donald Trump
a6669.title: US President
a6669.speech: Now demands reciprocity in trade, asking that African countries consider opening their markets to more American goods in exchange for continued benefits under AGOA.

a6669.speaker: Council on Foreign Relations (report)
a6669.name: Council on Foreign Relations (report)
a6669.speech: Said this could flood the continent with cheap American goods, and that the new president's current language suggests the trade programme, introduced in 2000 under former president Bill Clinton, is set to undergo a radical transformation: "The prospect of a protectionist trade agenda underscored by sweeping tariffs is proving a significant concern for many governments, and none - ally or otherwise - are seemingly safe. This growing anxiety raises questions about the possible scenarios facing Africans."

a6669.speaker: Femi Mimiko, professor of foreign policy at Obafemi Awolowo University
a6669.name: Femi Mimiko
a6669.title: professor of foreign policy at Obafemi Awolowo University
a6669.speech: Said Trump's second term will generally be unfavourable politically and economically for Nigeria and Africa, and that although his focus would be on undercutting China worldwide, including in Africa, President Trump might be "unwilling to offer some of the developmental goodies" that China will be more willing to provide: "Trump would latch onto bullying tactics. However, this may not work. This is why it is apposite and commendable that Nigeria has taken partner membership in BRICS, one organisation that promises to be a veritable bulwark against the imminent harassment of weaker nations of the Global South by the Trump administration. Beyond this, I expect the Trump administration to be generally noisy and unhinged, especially in its first two years - before the midterm elections. But by and large, my hunch is that American democratic institutions are going to hold up and frustrate many of the hifalutin but impracticable ideas Trump has been banding around."

a6719.speaker: Africa Sustainable Development Report 2025 (jointly produced by the African Union Commission, the UN Economic Commission for Africa, the African Development Bank and the UN Development Programme)
a6719.name: Africa Sustainable Development Report 2025 (jointly produced by the African Union Commission
a6719.title: the UN Economic Commission for Africa, the African Development Bank and the UN Development Programme)
a6719.speech: Disclosed that Nigeria has emerged as the third-largest African recipient of USAID development assistance, receiving $876m in 2024; that the Democratic Republic of Congo topped the list with $1.3bn, followed by Ethiopia with $1.25bn, ahead of South Sudan ($830m), Kenya ($824m), Mozambique ($756m) and Sudan ($694m); that the aid accounted for just 0.21 per cent of Nigeria’s GDP, the second-lowest ratio among the top ten beneficiaries, while South Sudan recorded the highest aid-to-GDP ratio at 6.05 per cent; and that the top ten beneficiaries across Africa received $8.1bn in USAID funding in 2024.

a6719.speaker: Africa Sustainable Development Report 2025 (African Union Commission, UNECA, AfDB, UNDP)
a6719.name: Africa Sustainable Development Report 2025 (African Union Commission
a6719.title: UNECA, AfDB, UNDP)
a6719.speech: Highlighted the uneven distribution of financing needs across African regions, stating: “At the subregional level, East and West Africa exhibit the largest financing needs and gaps, driven by the presence of some of the continent’s most populous countries, including Nigeria, Ethiopia, and the Democratic Republic of Congo. North and Southern Africa report smaller SDG financing gaps, reflecting their relatively higher levels of development and broader fiscal space.”

a6719.speaker: Punch newspaper
a6719.name: Punch newspaper
a6719.speech: Reported that the 2025 report emphasised that while aid flows remain vital, African countries must increase domestic resource mobilisation and enhance fiscal efficiency to bridge the vast financing gaps hindering progress towards the Sustainable Development Goals.

a6787.speaker: Youssouf Moussa Dawaleh, President of the Djibouti Chamber of Commerce
a6787.name: Youssouf Moussa Dawaleh
a6787.title: President of the Djibouti Chamber of Commerce
a6787.speech: In a brief address, stressed the current trend toward virtual meetings in a time of pandemic in order to maintain contact, communication and cross-border cooperation and to counter the interruptions caused by restrictive measures and the decline in physical business meetings: "This crisis, which has affected the whole world, has had a strong economic impact and has disrupted our way of life. It has also forced us to reassess our way of working and of interacting with others. Indeed, in order to stay in contact with our partners, the digital transformation of our entities has become an emergency solution to make up for the difficulties of the crisis and to continue commercial transactions. Until now, the use of digital technology within companies was often justified by the gains in effectiveness and efficiency in structuring and streamlining procedures, facilitating the transmission of messages, and broadening commercial relations ... that it allowed."

a6787.speaker: Youssouf Moussa Dawaleh, President of the Djibouti Chamber of Commerce
a6787.name: Youssouf Moussa Dawaleh
a6787.title: President of the Djibouti Chamber of Commerce
a6787.speech: Recalled that the exponential growth of digital technology and digitalisation has created a new situation, mentioned Djibouti's comparative advantage in the field of communication thanks to its modern infrastructure and the ICT cables passing through its waters, and underlined the country's role as a facilitator and regional point of entry for an economy focused on services: "Our country has a comparative advantage since, under the impetus of the Head of State Mr Ismail Omar Guelleh, the Republic of Djibouti has undertaken major investments in its telecommunications infrastructure, in particular intercontinental submarine cables. We welcome the development of this infrastructure, which remains to this day a vector of progress, growth and prosperity for any emerging country. Our country, whose economy has the particularity of being focused on the tertiary sector, has the resources and the potential to grow and create more jobs in this sector. We are indeed witnessing in recent times the development of a real dynamic in the field of start-ups, which must be supported and accompanied."

a6787.speaker: Youssouf Moussa Dawaleh, President of the Djibouti Chamber of Commerce
a6787.name: Youssouf Moussa Dawaleh
a6787.title: President of the Djibouti Chamber of Commerce
a6787.speech: Set out areas with strong growth potential, in particular technology and innovative start-ups as beacons of the development of Djibouti's private sector: "In this framework, and in order to allow this sector to boost employment in our country, to support technology incubators and the structures that accompany young innovative companies ... As the institution in charge of supporting businesses, we have planned, under the new term of office, to contribute to this support and to put the enterprise at the heart of our action, in particular through new services developed in collaboration with international partners such as the AFD, UNDP, the EU, USAID and, I hope, soon with the International Organisation of la Francophonie." Stated the objective of the economic operators the chamber represents: to access new opportunities and collaborate more with the International Organisation of la Francophonie.

a6787.speaker: Louise Mushikiwabo, Secretary General of the International Organisation of la Francophonie (OIF)
a6787.name: Louise Mushikiwabo
a6787.title: Secretary General of the International Organisation of la Francophonie (OIF)
a6787.speech: For her part welcomed the privileged relations the OIF maintains with Djibouti; presented the institution, recalling the very essence and founding of the Francophonie in 1970 - newly sovereign countries collaborating by drawing on the heritage of a shared working language - and unveiled a major project under way in Djibouti: the creation of a Regional Centre for the Teaching of French, which will serve the Horn of Africa and the Middle East. Listed the institution's immediate objectives, namely to identify needs in the Francophone world and to define the priorities and key actions to be undertaken with Djibouti, determining the most important points for Djibouti and the other members of the institution; closed her address by setting out the projects under way, the summits and the upcoming trade missions, saying the goal is to bring the Francophone world to Djibouti and make it a point of entry into the region, based on the Republic of Djibouti's motto of a land of exchange where languages and cultures meet.

a6873.speaker: David Greene, Acting US Ambassador to Nigeria
a6873.name: David Greene
a6873.title: Acting US Ambassador to Nigeria
a6873.speech: “It is an honour for me to lead the embassy at this time. It is such a consequential post and country. Let me wish Ramadan Karim to all those that are celebrating.” ; “The US-Nigeria relationship is such an important and vital one. The US and Nigeria are not just essential but also natural partners because we share so much in common. So, I am very proud of all we are doing. This mission actively supports so many shared agendas on peace and security, democratic governance, health outcomes, food security, climate change.”

a6873.speaker: David Greene, Acting US Ambassador to Nigeria
a6873.name: David Greene
a6873.title: Acting US Ambassador to Nigeria
a6873.speech: On the delay in confirming a substantive ambassador: “Well, it is the US Senate that must provide advice and consent on nomination of ambassadors. And you know it is not uncommon for there to be delays between the confirmation of an ambassador and other officers of the United States. So, in the interim, I will continue to work and advance US-Nigerian relations in the different fields we are cooperating.”

a6873.speaker: David Greene, Acting US Ambassador to Nigeria
a6873.name: David Greene
a6873.title: Acting US Ambassador to Nigeria
a6873.speech: “What we do as the US mission in Nigeria is of great benefit to both Nigerians and Americans. Of course we protect American citizens that are in Nigeria but we invest billion dollars a year roughly in development and humanitarian assistance. US businesses have invested over $5billion in Nigeria over the years. We have a two-way trade of $10bn a year, and all those engagements and investments are creating opportunities for Nigerian citizens; they are creating jobs and improving health outcomes.” ; “So, what we are doing together in this very important partnership has dividends for Nigerians and Americans; and quite frankly, beyond, because of Nigeria's very vital role as an important economic and security actor, not just in the continent but globally.”

a6873.speaker: David Greene, Acting US Ambassador to Nigeria
a6873.name: David Greene
a6873.title: Acting US Ambassador to Nigeria
a6873.speech: On the trade balance: “I think it is. Last year, our statistics for 2022 was a slight edge to Nigeria in terms of trade balance. I think that balanced trade figures to over $10bn a year. It speaks to how kind and symbiotic our partnership is, and all the different levels and ways we engage.” ; “You know there are bulk commodities we buy from each other. You also have tremendous trade and services. Look at what US firms are doing with the Nigerian creative and tech sector, for example, and you would see a trade relationship and investment that is really benefiting both Nigeria and the United States.”

a6873.speaker: David Greene, Acting US Ambassador to Nigeria
a6873.name: David Greene
a6873.title: Acting US Ambassador to Nigeria
a6873.speech: On agriculture and wheat: “I think we always look at trade as an opportunity for beneficial gains for everybody. And obviously, if we eliminate barriers to trade and allow the market to find its natural balance... there's great benefit as it creates wealth and job opportunities everywhere.” ; “I can't really speak specifically on wheat, but the agric sector is an area we invest very heavily through USAID's Feed the Future programme, which is intended to strengthen the productivity of Nigerian farmers.” ; “I was recently at the launch of a $22million five-year investment by the US Department of Agriculture in the cocoa value chain in six states that produce cocoa intended to enhance the reliability and income that farmers get, and to support processing and export.” ; “We are always looking for areas of collaboration. I think we can help because we are such a large agricultural producing country. We have the technical means to help Nigerian farmers produce more and enhance the value chain.” ; “These are areas where the US Department of Agriculture and USAID and other parts of our government have vast experience in trying to help with successful and enhanced agricultural production all over.” ; “We have an Office of Foreign Agricultural Service in Lagos, which works very closely with producers and policy makers across Nigeria to try and enhance Nigerian agriculture.”

a6873.speaker: David Greene, Acting US Ambassador to Nigeria
a6873.name: David Greene
a6873.title: Acting US Ambassador to Nigeria
a6873.speech: On the tech sector: “Absolutely, the tech sector is very exciting and vibrant. This is one of those areas I think the US-Nigeria relationship is very strong because of shared characteristics our two countries have. We are two great federal republics.” ; “Look at American tech firms like Google, Microsoft or Meta and Equinex and you would know that we are making enormous investments and creating jobs in Nigeria. Look at Nigerian firms like Flutterwave or Interswitch, which are some of Africa's tech giants.” ; “Some of Nigeria's biggest tech leaders like Flutterwave and Interswitch were founded by Nigerians who studied in the United States...” ; “I think we see the tech sector as a tremendous field of opportunity for economic growth, investment and job creation.” ; “there are challenges on regulators to make smart choices that are going to support and strengthen that sector so that it can grow and create jobs and bring prosperity but in a responsible way.”

a6873.speaker: David Greene, Acting US Ambassador to Nigeria
a6873.name: David Greene
a6873.title: Acting US Ambassador to Nigeria
a6873.speech: On media transformation and AI: “Well, I am not an expert on the media sector, but I do think the transformation of media globally is something the internet is driving at a very rapid clip.” ; “An example is Artificial Intelligence (AI)... There are lots of efforts to sort of establish the rules of the road on how we can use AI safely and responsibly. That's an area the US is really seeking, promoting and working closely with Nigeria as a partner... We have a very vested interest, not just in the successful AI sector but in a responsible one.”

a6873.speaker: David Greene, Acting US Ambassador to Nigeria
a6873.name: David Greene
a6873.title: Acting US Ambassador to Nigeria
a6873.speech: On Nigeria's economic reforms: “It is clear that this is a challenging moment in Nigeria's economy and for Nigerians. Certainly, we see and feel that.” ; “Part of what the United States does through its billion-dollar a year investment in development and humanitarian assistance is both to help lay the foundation for stronger economic growth... and through our humanitarian assistance, which is over $300million a year, to try and help the most vulnerable Nigerians.” ; “I will refer you to the Nigerian government for their views on their economic policies going forward. But we all know, for example, that fuel subsidy was blowing $10bn a year in the Nigerian budget; and most of the benefits of fuel subsidy were going to the richest Nigerians.” ; “Stabilising the exchange rate of the naira and dealing with fuel subsidy are obviously painful decisions that were put off for too long. We are trying to support these economic reforms by the Tinubu administration, hoping that it would lay the foundation for a stronger Nigerian economy for the future.” ; “in the previous environment, foreign companies were hesitant to invest because they weren't sure they were going to be able to repatriate their earnings...” ; “We are working with other partners and donors. The World Bank has been supporting palliatives for the poorest Nigerians.”

a6873.speaker: David Greene, Acting US Ambassador to Nigeria
a6873.name: David Greene
a6873.title: Acting US Ambassador to Nigeria
a6873.speech: On insecurity: “We take the insecurity issue very seriously. In any country, security is top in everybody's mind. If you don't have security you can't have a livelihood, you can't have a business, you can't have investment and you can't safely send your kids to school.” ; “By the way, I want to express my sympathy for the victims of violence and kidnapping in the North. It is heartbreaking. We certainly stand with victims of those crimes and want to see those folks returned and the perpetrators punished.”

a6873.speaker: David Greene, Acting US Ambassador to Nigeria
a6873.name: David Greene
a6873.title: Acting US Ambassador to Nigeria
a6873.speech: On Gaza and Israel: “I think it is important to remember that on October 7, Israel and Israelis were dehumanised in a way that is hard to contemplate – over 1,000 civilians were killed and over 200 kidnapped. We stand with Israel when it comes to making sure that such a horrible crime can never transpire again.” ; “President Biden has been in the lead on this, pressing Israel to take the actions it feels compelled to take in ways that minimise civilian harm.” ; “We are at the forefront of efforts to bring humanitarian assistance to Gaza, whether it is by land or air drops. We are investing right now in the construction of a pier so that humanitarian assistance can be brought in by sea.” ; “Of course there's great concern; any harm to civilians is of great concern to all of us. We feel very strongly that the international humanitarian law must be followed.” ; “It is important to remember that all these deaths and destruction are because Hamas as an organisation dedicated to the destruction of a UN member-state... launched a horrific attack against that state and provoked this whole conflagration.” ; “The United States has long been pushing for and supporting building coalitions to support a two-state solution...”

a6873.speaker: David Greene, Acting US Ambassador to Nigeria
a6873.name: David Greene
a6873.title: Acting US Ambassador to Nigeria
a6873.speech: On the US presidential election and its effect on relations: “I don't have a crystal.” ; “I can't really look into the future, but what I can say is that the US-Nigeria relationship is built on some key fundamentals; we are natural partners in so many ways.” ; “We have a 500,000 strong Nigerian Diaspora in the United States that binds our countries together. We have so much in common. Nigerian culture, food and film are everywhere in the United States these days.” ; “When I look at the shared values and history of the US and Nigeria, I see a very strong relationship, no matter what.”

a6873.speaker: David Greene, Acting US Ambassador to Nigeria
a6873.name: David Greene
a6873.title: Acting US Ambassador to Nigeria
a6873.speech: On high-level engagement: “I would say we have a tremendous high level engagement with Nigeria. Our presidents met at the G20 in India few months back. We have a steady stream of very senior US officials coming to Nigeria to engage.” ; “Secretary of State Blinken was just here six weeks ago, and that was his second-in-person. Add the virtual visit he did shortly after he took office. That speaks to how important the US-Nigeria relationship is and how we are investing in it in so many different ways.”

a6932.speaker: Health technician contracted by the agency implementing US-funded programmes (anonymous), Maputo health unit
a6932.name: Health technician contracted by the agency implementing US-funded programmes (anonymous)
a6932.title: Maputo health unit
a6932.speech: Said, on condition of anonymity, that they are not permitted to provide any HIV prevention or family planning services until further orders: "We are no longer providing PrEP, for example, that has stopped. And it is complicated when someone comes looking for those services and we tell them we cannot provide them."

a6932.speaker: Ministry of Health (MISAU) official at the same health unit (anonymous)
a6932.name: Ministry of Health (MISAU) official at the same health unit (anonymous)
a6932.speech: Said that in some cases it is possible for prevention or planning methods to be provided to citizens, as long as it is through MISAU funding and not through foreign funding organisations: "Here, we sometimes give PrEP. What is wanted is for the person to be attended to by an internal staff member, because the government still intends to keep these programmes, which means we are not prohibited."

a6932.speaker: Observatório Cidadão para Saúde (Citizen Health Observatory)
a6932.name: Observatório Cidadão para Saúde (Citizen Health Observatory)
a6932.speech: Understands that the suspension of funding, announced on 20 January and later extended to emergency matters, could have much more negative impacts on public health.

a6932.speaker: António Mathe, coordinator for participation at the Observatório Cidadão para Saúde
a6932.name: António Mathe
a6932.title: coordinator for participation at the Observatório Cidadão para Saúde
a6932.speech: "This means for example that HIV, TB, paediatric ART, family planning, malaria and nutrition and key population programmes could be affected by the halting of services" ; Proposes as a possible solution - while acknowledging it is not a plan applicable in the short term - the mobilisation of internal resources through alternative sources of financing, new fiscal space, a sovereign fund and through the extractive industry, to address the gaps that the withdrawal of foreign financing could create in public health in Mozambique.

a6932.speaker: US Embassy in Mozambique (official data)
a6932.name: US Embassy in Mozambique (official data)
a6932.speech: According to official data from the American embassy in Mozambique, with PEPFAR support more than 1.8 million people receive anti-retroviral treatment.

a6949.speaker: Dumisani Msibi, Group Managing Director of the Eswatini Development Finance Corporation (FINCORP)
a6949.name: Dumisani Msibi
a6949.title: Group Managing Director of the Eswatini Development Finance Corporation (FINCORP)
a6949.speech: Announced that FINCORP has sustained more than 15,000 jobs in the past 15 years through its financing initiatives, and said the corporation remained committed to empowering entrepreneurs and building communities through access to finance and training.

a6949.speaker: Dumisani Msibi, Group Managing Director of FINCORP
a6949.name: Dumisani Msibi
a6949.title: Group Managing Director of FINCORP
a6949.speech: Revealed that FINCORP had injected E300,000 into this year's business shower, bringing the total investment into Junior Achievement programmes to about E1 million, with E600,000 invested in the same initiative over the past two years alone ; "These resources are not just numbers. They are transforming lives, uplifting families, and empowering communities across the Kingdom." ; disclosed that about E1.5 billion is currently circulating in the hands of Emaswati entrepreneurs supported by FINCORP's products and services ; "This is capital that is developing individuals economically and ensuring that their families and communities' benefit."

a6949.speaker: Dumisani Msibi, Group Managing Director of FINCORP
a6949.name: Dumisani Msibi
a6949.title: Group Managing Director of FINCORP
a6949.speech: Highlighted the findings of the 2023 Blended FinScope MSME Survey and said the statistics demonstrated the central role played by micro, small and medium enterprises in the national economy; pointed out that the MSME Policy 2024-2029 had acknowledged FINCORP's contribution in addressing financing barriers, especially for micro and rural enterprises.

a6949.speaker: Dumisani Msibi, Group Managing Director of FINCORP
a6949.name: Dumisani Msibi
a6949.title: Group Managing Director of FINCORP
a6949.speech: "Young people are the heartbeat of our nation, yet too often, they face one of the greatest barriers to entrepreneurship and access to finance due to lack of collateral." ; explained that FINCORP had signed an agreement with the Centre for Financial Inclusion (CFI) to provide additional support for young entrepreneurs, covering 20 per cent per borrower and supporting loans of up to E250,000 for youth between the ages of 18 and 35 ; "Finance alone is not enough, and we believe that this initiative is more than just a program, but a Launchpad for young entrepreneurs." ; said E50,000 will go directly to support the top five winning businesses with E10,000 seed capital each to help them launch their new ventures.

a6949.speaker: Dumisani Msibi, Group Managing Director of FINCORP
a6949.name: Dumisani Msibi
a6949.title: Group Managing Director of FINCORP
a6949.speech: Said the Citizen Economic Empowerment Act and the Business One Stop Shop (BOSS) had set the stage for MSMEs, especially youth-led businesses, to enter the market with fewer barriers, greater support and more confidence ; "The future of Eswatini's economy cannot be reinvigorated by a few large companies here and there, but by thousands of existing and future entrepreneurs including those gathered here today." ; reassured young entrepreneurs that FINCORP remained committed to expanding partnerships, innovating services and walking alongside them ; "When you succeed, communities prosper; when you thrive, the nation thrives."

a6949.speaker: 2023 Blended FinScope MSME Survey
a6949.name: 2023 Blended FinScope MSME Survey
a6949.speech: Showed that Eswatini is home to approximately 70,000 enterprises employing over 90,000 people and contributing nearly 50 percent of the country's gross domestic product (GDP).

a6949.speaker: MSME Policy 2024-2029 (Eswatini)
a6949.name: MSME Policy 2024-2029 (Eswatini)
a6949.speech: Acknowledged FINCORP's contribution in addressing financing barriers, especially for micro and rural enterprises.

a6949.speaker: Manqoba Khumalo, Minister of Commerce, Industry and Trade (Eswatini)
a6949.name: Manqoba Khumalo
a6949.title: Minister of Commerce, Industry and Trade (Eswatini)
a6949.speech: Described the JA Business Shower as instrumental in enhancing MSME growth and encouraging investment, and commended Junior Achievement Eswatini for creating opportunities for young people to participate in meaningful economic activity during the Eswatini International Trade Fair.

a6949.speaker: Manqoba Khumalo, Minister of Commerce, Industry and Trade (Eswatini)
a6949.name: Manqoba Khumalo
a6949.title: Minister of Commerce, Industry and Trade (Eswatini)
a6949.speech: Said youth empowerment remained a government priority, stressing that platforms such as the trade fair offered traders the opportunity to promote themselves in the local market ; "The EITF serves as an excellent platform for traders to introduce or promote themselves, complemented by various value-adding activities such as business seminars that run throughout the duration of the show."

a6949.speaker: Manqoba Khumalo, Minister of Commerce, Industry and Trade (Eswatini)
a6949.name: Manqoba Khumalo
a6949.title: Minister of Commerce, Industry and Trade (Eswatini)
a6949.speech: Assured young entrepreneurs that government support would continue ; "Government shall continue to support JA Eswatini through an annual subvention of E500 000 for promoting youth MSMEs and cooperatives in schools and out of school" ; explained that the Ministry of Economic Planning and Development had worked closely with his ministry to ensure financial support for programmes such as JA financial literacy and entrepreneurship, as well as cooperatives development; and encouraged young people to make use of existing support mechanisms including the Youth Enterprise Revolving Fund, Informal Traders Revolving Fund, Regional Development Fund, the E45 million MSME Revolving Fund, Women Micro Finance Revolving Fund, Eswatini Agricultural Development Fund, Small Scale Enterprise Loan Guarantee Scheme and the Export Credit Guarantee Scheme.

a6949.speaker: Phetsile Masilela, Executive Director of JA Eswatini
a6949.name: Phetsile Masilela
a6949.title: Executive Director of JA Eswatini
a6949.speech: Said the annual government subvention had enabled the organisation to implement financial literacy and entrepreneurship training for both in-school and out-of-school youth, and noted that the support came at a time when JA Eswatini was affected by the termination of USAID grants to the country.

a6949.speaker: Phetsile Masilela, Executive Director of JA Eswatini
a6949.name: Phetsile Masilela
a6949.title: Executive Director of JA Eswatini
a6949.speech: Said JA would host a Business Masterclass facilitated by different stakeholders; revealed that 35 applications had been received from young entrepreneurs seeking to pitch their businesses for seed capital support through the business shower, out of which 10 business plans were shortlisted with five set to receive funding as determined by judges; and emphasised that the business shower had grown into a platform where youth could not only access financial support but also gain mentorship and skills that would allow them to grow sustainable enterprises.

a6949.speaker: Organisers of the JA Business Shower
a6949.name: Organisers of the JA Business Shower
a6949.speech: Expressed hope that more young people would seize the opportunity to position themselves as the next generation of business leaders.

a7014.speaker: Ballotti (National Youth Council)
a7014.name: Ballotti (National Youth Council)
a7014.speech: Warned of instability over the disputed NYC elections, saying conducting elections amid violence, unresolved disputes and uncertainty regarding compliance would have risked producing a contested outcome and further instability within the National Youth Council.

a7014.speaker: MPs supporting the Petroleum Amendment Bill, National Assembly of Namibia
a7014.name: MPs supporting the Petroleum Amendment Bill
a7014.title: National Assembly of Namibia
a7014.speech: Pointed out that the draft legislation will improve oversight, attract investment and support local content and skills development.

a7014.speaker: Elijah Ngurare, Prime Minister of Namibia
a7014.name: Elijah Ngurare
a7014.title: Prime Minister of Namibia
a7014.speech: Informed the National Assembly that legislation to regulate "Order with Me" businesses will soon be introduced in parliament to support young entrepreneurs who are currently restricted from operating freely.

a7014.speaker: Government of Namibia
a7014.name: Government of Namibia
a7014.speech: Has outlined reforms aimed at removing the fuel premium currently paid by consumers and improving the structure of fuel imports in Namibia; has also directed that the issues of housing and sanitation be considered for declaration as a state of emergency.

a7014.speaker: Several Members of Parliament, National Assembly of Namibia
a7014.name: Several Members of Parliament
a7014.title: National Assembly of Namibia
a7014.speech: Questioned the structure, risks and implications of the proposed fuel supply arrangements.

a7014.speaker: Saara Kuugongelwa-Amadhila, Speaker of the National Assembly of Namibia
a7014.name: Saara Kuugongelwa-Amadhila
a7014.title: Speaker of the National Assembly of Namibia
a7014.speech: Said the National Assembly is not just renaming rooms and halls within but is breathing life into Namibia's shared history and common purpose by bestowing the names of forebearers upon the spaces where democracy is anchored.

a7014.speaker: Members of the National Council of Namibia
a7014.name: Members of the National Council of Namibia
a7014.speech: Have urged the government to settle outstanding payments owed to veterans who are still alive, as many reached advanced age; the MPs have also proposed an amendment to the current law regarding the transfer of inheritance of the projects.

a7014.speaker: Members of the National Council of Namibia
a7014.name: Members of the National Council of Namibia
a7014.speech: Have raised concerns over delayed service delivery in the justice system, urging more magistrates' courts in regions to speed up cases.

a7047.speaker: Ambassador António Sanchez-Benedito Gaspar, EU representative in Mozambique
a7047.name: Ambassador António Sanchez-Benedito Gaspar
a7047.title: EU representative in Mozambique
a7047.speech: Announced that the European Union has guaranteed €25 million for humanitarian assistance to the approximately 300,000 people displaced internally by terrorist activity in northern Cabo Delgado province, part of a total of €50 million. “We, as the European Union, are now beginning a new cycle of programming for our development aid, in which Cabo Delgado will occupy a central place,” Ambassador Sanchez Benedito said.

a7047.speaker: Celso Correia, Mozambican Minister of Agriculture and Rural Development
a7047.name: Celso Correia
a7047.title: Mozambican Minister of Agriculture and Rural Development
a7047.speech: “We were here to discuss and share relevant information and to build a coherent strategy that responds to the challenges in the northern region of the country. This is the work we have been doing, and today we have taken another step,” Minister Correia explained.

a7047.speaker: Celso Correia, Mozambican Minister of Agriculture and Rural Development
a7047.name: Celso Correia
a7047.title: Mozambican Minister of Agriculture and Rural Development
a7047.speech: The minister highlighted the role of the EU, stressing that the bloc is an important strategic partner for the country.

a7047.speaker: Antonio Sánchez-Benedito Gaspar (@SBeneditoEU), Twitter post
a7047.name: Antonio Sánchez-Benedito Gaspar (@SBeneditoEU)
a7047.title: Twitter post
a7047.speech: “We welcome the Government’s commitment, expressed by Minister Correia, to ‘never bend nor mortgage the development of the country on account of the insurgents’ in #CaboDelgado. The #EU and member states are committed to supporting/collaborating for the security and well-being of people today and in the future.”

a7088.speaker: Human Rights Watch (World Report 2025)
a7088.name: Human Rights Watch (World Report 2025)
a7088.speech: Paints an alarming picture of the human rights situation in Central Africa, highlighting a significant deterioration of fundamental freedoms in the region over the course of 2024 after examining human rights practices in more than 100 countries in its 546-page report; says wartime abuses are commonplace and testify to a lack of accountability in the region; reports that in Rwanda and the Central African Republic the authorities orchestrated “politically motivated prosecutions” to silence dissenting voices; that in Chad and Rwanda the general elections took place in a climate that was “neither free nor fair”; that in Burundi, ahead of the 2025 elections, “the authorities restricted the political space of the opposition”; that clashes in North Kivu province in the Democratic Republic of Congo caused the massive displacement of “2.5 million people”; that in Chad “more than 700,000 people have fled to the country to escape the armed conflict in Sudan”, with belligerents systematically hindering the delivery of humanitarian aid; that a historic trial in Rwanda led to the conviction of prison officials for acts of torture at Rubavu prison; and that in Chad the security forces “killed at least 11 people in a post-election shooting in May”.

a7088.speaker: Lewis Mudge, Central Africa director at Human Rights Watch
a7088.name: Lewis Mudge
a7088.title: Central Africa director at Human Rights Watch
a7088.speech: “Governments across Central Africa have repressed basic rights and freedoms, notably during elections and referendums, which raises concerns about governments' efforts to monopolise power.”

a7088.speaker: Tirana Hassan, executive director of Human Rights Watch (introductory essay)
a7088.name: Tirana Hassan
a7088.title: executive director of Human Rights Watch (introductory essay)
a7088.speech: Stresses that the regional situation forms part of a worrying global context, describing a world in which “governments have repressed, arrested and wrongfully imprisoned political opponents, activists and journalists”, while armed groups and government forces have multiplied abuses against civilian populations.

a7088.speaker: Human Rights Watch (call to governments)
a7088.name: Human Rights Watch (call to governments)
a7088.speech: Calls on the governments of Central Africa to honour their international commitments and to take concrete measures to protect fundamental freedoms, particularly in election periods; also insists on the need to strengthen the protection of civilians in conflict zones and to prosecute those responsible for abuses, regardless of their position in the hierarchy.

a7104.speaker: South Korean authorities
a7104.name: South Korean authorities
a7104.speech: According to the authorities, the crash of flight JJA-2216, which was flying from Bangkok to Muan, one of the deadliest in South Korea's history, occurred on Sunday at 09:03 (00:03 GMT).

a7104.speaker: Lee Jeong-hyun, head of the Muan fire station
a7104.name: Lee Jeong-hyun
a7104.title: head of the Muan fire station
a7104.speech: "The cause of the accident is presumed to be a collision with birds combined with unfavourable weather conditions. However, the exact cause will be announced at the conclusion of an investigation," he said at a press briefing.

a7104.speaker: MBC (local television channel) / Flightradar (specialist site)
a7104.name: MBC (local television channel) / Flightradar (specialist site)
a7104.speech: A video broadcast by the local channel MBC shows the aircraft - a Boeing 737-8AS that entered service in 2009, according to the specialist site Flightradar - landing with smoke escaping from its engines; the plane strikes a wall at the end of the runway and is immediately engulfed in flames.

a7104.speaker: Local fire official (anonymous)
a7104.name: Local fire official (anonymous)
a7104.speech: "The passengers were ejected from the plane during the collision with a barrier, which left them little chance of survival," he said during a meeting with the victims' families, adding: "The plane is almost entirely destroyed and identifying the deceased is proving difficult."

a7104.speaker: AFP photographer
a7104.name: AFP photographer
a7104.speech: Saw numerous emergency service vehicles and dozens of firefighters busy around the plane's carcass, completely burnt out except for the tail.

a7104.speaker: Choi Sang-mok, acting Head of State of South Korea
a7104.name: Choi Sang-mok
a7104.title: acting Head of State of South Korea
a7104.speech: "All the agencies concerned (...) must mobilise all available resources to rescue people," he ordered in a statement; his office announced that he chaired an emergency government meeting and is due to travel to Muan on Sunday afternoon.

a7104.speaker: Boeing
a7104.name: Boeing
a7104.speech: Said it was in contact with Jeju Air and was "ready to support them".

a7104.speaker: Jeju Air (statement published on its social media)
a7104.name: Jeju Air (statement published on its social media)
a7104.speech: "Jeju Air will do everything in its power to deal with this accident. We offer our sincere apologies."

a7209.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa
a7209.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a7209.title: President of South Africa
a7209.speech: Acknowledged that the security cluster was caught napping and was not adequately prepared; sent a stern message to those behind the violent acts who have sought to provoke a "popular insurrection", saying that law enforcement was working on bringing them to book: "It is clear now that the events of the past week were nothing less than a deliberate, coordinated and well-planned attack on our democracy. The constitutional order of our country is under threat. The current instability and ongoing incitement to violence constitute a direct contravention of the Constitution and the rule of law. These actions are intended to cripple the economy, cause social instability and severely weaken - or even dislodge - the democratic state."

a7209.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa
a7209.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a7209.title: President of South Africa
a7209.speech: "To stabilise the country, we have massively increased the numbers of law enforcement and security personnel on the ground in Gauteng and KwaZulu-Natal. I have authorised the deployment of 25 000 members of the SA National Defence Force to support the work of the police."

a7209.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa
a7209.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a7209.title: President of South Africa
a7209.speech: Said the SA Police Service is investigating 131 cases of murder and has opened inquest dockets in respect of 81 deaths.

a7209.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa
a7209.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a7209.title: President of South Africa
a7209.speech: Announced measures to remedy the situation: government is in the process of providing immediate food relief to households, prioritising areas affected by the looting and where people have no access to food; five provincial departments of social development and the SA Social Security Agency will use their remaining budget in the Social Relief of Distress programme to provide food parcels, cash and food vouchers; the Solidarity Fund has established a Humanitarian Crisis Relief Fund to assist those in greatest need; and small businesses, including those in townships and rural areas, will be assisted.

a7209.speaker: Government of South Africa
a7209.name: Government of South Africa
a7209.speech: Revealed this week that 12 people are under investigation for their involvement in instigating the riots in the country, and that one of them has already been taken into police custody.

a7433.speaker: Volodymyr Zelenskiy, President of Ukraine
a7433.name: Volodymyr Zelenskiy
a7433.title: President of Ukraine
a7433.speech: In a speech to parliament, said he expected his new government to increase the share of domestic weapons on Ukraine’s battlefield to 50% from 40% within six months ; also singled out deregulation and expanding economic co-operation with allies as other key aims of the biggest government reshuffle since Russia’s February 2022 invasion ; has tasked Yulia Svyrydenko with boosting domestic weapons production and reviving Ukraine’s loan-dependent economy.

a7433.speaker: Volodymyr Zelenskiy, President of Ukraine
a7433.name: Volodymyr Zelenskiy
a7433.title: President of Ukraine
a7433.speech: Addressing lawmakers on Thursday, said further deals with the U.S. would be forthcoming but did not offer any specific details.

a7433.speaker: Yulia Svyrydenko, Prime Minister of Ukraine
a7433.name: Yulia Svyrydenko
a7433.title: Prime Minister of Ukraine
a7433.speech: Pledged to move “swiftly and decisively” ; “War leaves no room for delay,” she wrote on X ; “Our priorities for the first six months are clear: reliable supply for the army, expansion of domestic weapons production, and boosting the technological strength of our defense forces.”

a7433.speaker: Yulia Svyrydenko, Prime Minister of Ukraine
a7433.name: Yulia Svyrydenko
a7433.title: Prime Minister of Ukraine
a7433.speech: Said her government would launch a full audit of public finances to achieve “real savings”, as well as accelerate large-scale privatisations and help entrepreneurs.

a7433.speaker: Denys Shmyhal, former prime minister, appointed defence minister
a7433.name: Denys Shmyhal
a7433.title: former prime minister, appointed defence minister
a7433.speech: “This team is time-tested,” Shmyhal wrote on Thursday. “Ahead are new tasks, challenges and a high level of responsibility.”

a7433.speaker: Ukrainian officials
a7433.name: Ukrainian officials
a7433.speech: Officials have said they could face a shortfall of about $19 billion next year.

a7433.speaker: Some opposition lawmakers
a7433.name: Some opposition lawmakers
a7433.speech: Voiced scepticism about the new government’s ability to remain independent of Zelenskiy’s administration, which wields significant wartime powers under Ukraine’s constitution.

a7433.speaker: Yaroslav Zheleznyak of the Holos party
a7433.name: Yaroslav Zheleznyak of the Holos party
a7433.speech: “They will be told by the president’s office what they should really do,” he wrote.
